articles.title: Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis on bench as England squad named for clash vs France after opening defeat
articles.summary: England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am kick-off BST) for second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; England play Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on October 30; England Women began their campaign with big win vs Wales in Perth
articles.body:
AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening-game defeat to Tonga.

Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while Mikey Lewis returns to the bench after missing out on a place in the squad last time out.

As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on.

Last weekend against Tonga, Welsby and Warrington Wolves winger Matty Ashton were the unused substitutes. Wigan Warriors speedster Zach Eckersley was initially selected to start again, until Ashton replaced him on Thursday.

For France, Toulouse playmaker Thomas Lacans has been promoted to start at five-eighth with Cesar Rouge moving to the bench.

Romeo Tropis comes in at centre, so Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet pushes out to the wing and Leo Darrelatour makes way.

Skipper Ben Garcia moves from hooker to lock and Amir Bourouh joins the starting side at No 9. A change in the front-row sees Julian Bousquet come in at prop for Lambert Belmas, who goes to the bench.

England: AJ Brimson, Dom Young, Hugo Savala, Herbie Farnworth, Matty Ashton, George Williams, Harry Smith, Max King, Brad O'Neill, Luke Thompson, Junior Nsemba, Kai Pearce-Paul, Victor Radley.

Interchange: Jez Litten, Ben Currie, Ethan Havard, Sam Walters, Jack Welsby, Mikey Lewis.

France: Arthur Mourgue, Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet, Latrell Siegwalt, Roméo Tropis, Benjamin Laguerre, Thomas Lacans, Théo Fages, Romain Navarrete, Amir Bourouh, Julian Bousquet, Arthur Romano, Mathieu Jussaume, Benjamin Garcia (c).

Interchange: César Rougé, Lambert Belmas, Mathieu Cozza, Louis Grossemy.

Teenager Foubister to start as England Women face Australia

For the England Women side, head coach Stuart Barrow has made a shock selection call at half-back, calling in 19-year-old Jenna Foubister to wear the No 7 and partner Isabel Rowe in the halves against Australia on Saturday.

Foubister was named Woman of Steel after a standout year in the Super League and came off the bench in last week's win over Wales. Georgia Roche shifts to the interchange as a result.

Molly Jones has been named to replace Georgia Wilson in the centres while Liv Wood steps in at prop in place of Mary Coleman. Lucie Sams is the new face on the interchange.

For Australia, Dragons recruit Makenzie Weale and former sevens star Sariah Paki are in line for Test debuts after being named on the interchange for the clash with England.

Coach Jess Skinner has made a handful of changes to the side that defeated Samoa last week, with Abbi Church coming in on the wing and Julia Robinson shifting to centre. Jess Sergis has been rested. Tiana Penitani Gray will line up in the back-row with Kezie Apps rested, while Quincy Dodd has also come on to the bench.

England Women: Fran Goldthorpe, Anna Davies, Molly Jones, Connie Boyd, Amelia Brown, Izzy Rowe, Jenna Foubister, Liv Wood, Keara Bennett, Hollie-Mae Dodd, Jasmin Strange, Eva Hunter, Megan Williams.

Interchange: Jodie Cunningham, Vicky Whitfield, Georgia Roche, Lucie Sams.

articles.title: Los motivos de los cuatro robos a futbolistas en la misma semana
articles.standfirst: Vicenç Guillén, CEO y cofundador de MĀRS Seguridad y antiguo mando policial en unidades especiales da las claves en el programa 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA
articles.summary: Vicenç Guillén, CEO y cofundador de MĀRS Seguridad y antiguo mando policial en unidades especiales da las claves en el programa 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA
articles.body: Cuatro futbolistas profesionales han sufrido robos en sus viviendas en apenas una semana. Algunos de los asaltos se produjeron mientras estaban disputando partidos y otros, con sus casas aparentemente vacías. El botín incluye joyas, relojes y bolsos de lujo, pero uno de los casos ha ido mucho más allá de las pérdidas económicas: Sergio Rico y su familia sufrieron un violento asalto en su domicilio de Sevilla. ¿Qué hay detrás de estos robos? ¿Cómo seleccionan los delincuentes sus objetivos? Vicenç Guillén, CEO y cofundador de MĀRS Seguridad y antiguo mando policial en unidades especiales, respondió a estas preguntas en ‘Otra Ronda’, el programa de Radio MARCA presentado por Carlos Vicente ‘Chitu’. "Los robos no son al azar, hay una vigilancia previa, hay obtención de información y se miran diferentes casas", explicó el especialista, que cuenta con 15 años de experiencia como mando en unidades especiales de la policía. El caso más grave de esta sucesión de asaltos es el de Sergio Rico y su pareja, Alba Silva. Cinco hombres encapuchados y armados irrumpieron en su vivienda de Bollullos de la Mitación, en Sevilla, cuando la familia se encontraba cenando. En el interior también estaban sus dos hijos pequeños, la madre de Alba Silva y una empleada del hogar. Los asaltantes maniataron al guardameta y amenazaron a los presentes para hacerse con el botín. Según las informaciones publicadas, se llevaron joyas y relojes de lujo valorados en al menos 600.000 euros. El asalto estuvo marcado por la violencia y el miedo vivido por toda la familia. El episodio refleja una de las principales preocupaciones de Guillén: que los delincuentes no solo buscan objetos de valor, sino que pueden llegar a actuar cuando saben que los propietarios están en casa. "Imagínate el caso ahora de Sevilla. Que te entren con tu familia, que te tengan allí, que te aten, armas, gente con pasamontañas", señaló durante la entrevista. El experto también advirtió de las consecuencias psicológicas que puede dejar una experiencia de este tipo, especialmente en los niños. "Cualquier ruido que escuchen, cualquier cosa, los niños se van a asustar", explicó. El extremo brasileño del Betis denunció un robo en su domicilio el miércoles 14 de octubre, coincidiendo con el partido de Champions League frente al Oporto, disputado en el estadio de La Cartuja. El encuentro, que terminó con victoria verdiblanca por 3-2, suponía una noche especial para el equipo y su afición, pero acabó marcada por lo sucedido en la vivienda del futbolista. Antony expresó su indignación a través de las redes sociales y lamentó que una noche que prometía ser brillante terminara convertida en una experiencia de rabia, tristeza y frustración. El jugador también puso el acento en la sensación de inseguridad que deja una intrusión en el hogar. La coincidencia entre el asalto y el partido ilustra uno de los riesgos que Guillén identifica en este tipo de delitos: la posibilidad de conocer de antemano cuándo una vivienda va a quedarse vacía. "Los días de partido, en algunos de los casos ya ha coincidido así", explicó el especialista, que también señaló los periodos vacacionales como momentos delicados para la seguridad de los futbolistas. El centrocampista del Celta también fue víctima de un robo en su vivienda de Nigrán, en Pontevedra. Los ladrones accedieron al inmueble durante la madrugada del martes 20 de octubre y sustrajeron joyas y dinero en efectivo, cuyo valor no se ha concretado públicamente. Según las informaciones publicadas, la vivienda estaba aparentemente vacía en el momento de los hechos. La Guardia Civil investiga el asalto y otros robos registrados en el municipio durante las últimas semanas, aunque por el momento no se ha confirmado que todos estén relacionados. El caso vuelve a poner sobre la mesa la importancia de conocer los hábitos de los propietarios y sus horarios. Para Guillén, la preparación de estos delitos puede incluir tanto la vigilancia física de las viviendas como la recopilación de información en internet. "No están pasando por ahí en una casa potente y deciden vigilar la entrada", explicó. Según su análisis, los grupos organizados estudian diferentes objetivos antes de decidir dónde actuar. El portero del Villarreal Peter Gulácsi sufrió otro asalto en su vivienda de la urbanización Los Monasterios, en Puçol, Valencia. Varios encapuchados entraron en el chalet durante la madrugada del 13 de octubre, cuando el guardameta húngaro se encontraba con su familia. Los asaltantes amenazaron con un arma al futbolista y a su esposa y les obligaron a abrir la caja fuerte. El botín rondaría los 200.000 euros e incluiría relojes Rolex y bolsos de firmas de lujo como Chanel y Hermès. Según las informaciones publicadas, los ladrones permanecieron en la vivienda alrededor de 40 minutos y el sistema de alarma estaba desconectado. El impacto del asalto también tuvo consecuencias deportivas: Gulácsi no estuvo disponible para el encuentro de Champions League ante el Nápoles y se reincorporó posteriormente a los entrenamientos. Para Guillén, los cuatro casos ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de ir más allá de la instalación de una alarma. La metodología de MĀRS Seguridad comienza con un estudio de la familia, su exposición pública, las características de la vivienda y las personas que acceden habitualmente al domicilio. "Nuestra metodología de trabajo es inteligencia aplicada a la seguridad", explicó en Radio MARCA. El experto insistió especialmente en la información que puede obtenerse a través de las redes sociales. Fotografías de relojes, bolsos, estancias de la vivienda o publicaciones de vacaciones en tiempo real pueden ofrecer pistas a quienes buscan un objetivo. "Donde tú a lo mejor quieres enseñar un bolso o un reloj, ellos lo que están viendo es cuánto de vulnerable es esa casa", advirtió. Por eso, recomendó evitar publicar desplazamientos en tiempo real y compartir las imágenes una vez finalizados los viajes. También destacó la importancia de controlar quién entra en las viviendas, incluidos los profesionales encargados de las reformas y el mantenimiento. Otro de los aspectos destacados por Guillén fue la necesidad de detectar una intrusión desde el perímetro de la vivienda. Los sistemas de analítica de vídeo, explicó, pueden permitir activar mecanismos de respuesta cuando se detecta a una persona en el jardín, en lugar de limitarse a grabar lo ocurrido. "Lo que tenemos que buscar y el objetivo es que en cuanto pisen un jardín, a nosotros ya se nos activen todos los mecanismos", afirmó. La prevención, sin embargo, no depende únicamente de la tecnología. También requiere protocolos, comunicación constante y concienciación por parte de los propietarios.

articles.body: Asian Para Games Live: Para Archery | Recurve Mixed Team – Harvinder Singh-Bhawna Finish Fourth Harvinder Singh and Bhawna miss out on a medal after losing 4-5 to Iran in a shoot-off. The Indian pair lead 4-2 but score 31 in the final end, allowing Iran to level the contest with 34 points. Both teams score 18 in the shoot-off, but Iran prevail by hitting the 10-ring. India's para archery campaign ends with six medals, including gold in men's doubles and silver in women's doubles in recurve archery..Asian Para Games Live: Para Shooting | Women's 50m 3P SH1 – Mona Agarwal Wins Second Gold With World Record Mona Agarwal clinches her second gold medal at the Games, setting a new world record of 357.5 points in the women's 50m 3P SH1 event. She finishes 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, who takes silver. Mona had earlier won gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event. Meanwhile, Avani Lekhara finishes fourth after slipping from the top two following the prone position during the standing series..Asian Para Games Live: India cross 100 medals; sports minister congratulates .Asian Para Games Live: Para Athletics | Men's Javelin Throw F37/38 – Haney Wins Gold With World Record Haney clinches gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 with a world-record effort of 60.49m in the F37 category on his final attempt. He adds a second medal to his Asian Para Games tally after previously winning bronze in the discus throw..Asian Para Games Live: Para Athletics | Men's 400m T64 – Sandeep Wins Gold With World Record Sandeep clinches gold in the men's 400m T64 final with a time of 52.28 seconds, setting a new T44 world record and surpassing Saudi Arabia's Nour Alsana. India's Ajay Kumar also reaches the podium, winning bronze in 53.61 seconds to secure a double medal finish for the country..Asian Para Games Live: India touches 100-medal mark .Asian Para Games Live: Para Badminton | Women's Singles SH6 – Nithya Sre Wins Silver Nithya Sre claims silver in the women's singles SH6 event after losing to China's Fengmei Li 12-21, 13-21 in the final. Naveen dominates the opening game before holding off his opponent in the second to secure another gold medal for India..Asian Para Games Live: Para Athletics | Women's Long Jump T47 – Nimisha Chakkungalparambil Wins Silver Nimisha Chakkungalparambil wins silver in the women's long jump T47 with a best effort of 5.37m. Sri Lanka's Dhananjana takes gold with a Games-record jump of 5.52m. Nimisha, who won gold at the previous edition, adds another medal to her Asian Para Games tally..Asian Para Games Live: Para Athletics | Men's Discus Throw F11 – Praveen Sharma Finishes Fourth Praveen Sharma finishes fourth in the men's discus throw F11 with a best effort of 30.64m. Iran dominates the event, sweeping all three medals to complete a podium clean sweep..Asian Para Games Live: Para Badminton | Men's Singles SL3 – Nitesh Kumar Wins Gold, Pramod Bhagat Takes Silver Nitesh Kumar defeats compatriot Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in straight games to win gold in the men's singles SL3 final. Pramod settles for silver as India secures a 1-2 finish in the event..Asian Para Games Live: Para Archery | Men's Doubles Recurve – Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi Win Gold India's Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi clinch gold in the men's doubles recurve event, defeating China 5-1 in the final. After sharing the opening set 35-35, the Indian duo win the next two sets 37-36 and 38-36 to secure India's first gold medal of the day..Asian Para Games Live: Para Athletics | Men's 1500m T46 – Parmod Retains Silver Parmod wins silver in the men's 1500m T46, clocking 4:09.65 to finish second. He retains the silver medal he won at the Hangzhou edition three years ago, adding another podium finish for India in para-athletics..Asian Para Games Live: Para Archery | Women's Doubles Recurve – Bhawna and Pooja Win Silver India's Bhawna and Pooja settle for silver in the women's doubles recurve event after losing 0-6 to China in the gold medal match. The Indian pair go down 31-38, 30-35, 29-39 across three sets as China clinch gold with a stronger shooting performance..Asian Para Games Live: Para Badminton | Women's Singles SU5 – Thulasimathi Murugesan Wins Silver Thulasimathi Murugesan settles for silver in the women's singles SU5 event after losing to China's Qiuxia Yang 18-21, 11-21 in the final..Asian Para Games 2026: Where India stands in medal tally India enjoyed its best day at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Thursday, winning 26 medals, including seven golds, to reclaim fourth place in the standings. The haul took India's overall tally to 88 medals — 21 gold, 26 silver and 41 bronze — with para-athletics continuing to lead the country's charge..Asian Para Games 2026: India's tally swells to 88 India's tally swelled to 88 at the Asian Para Games on Thursday. Sheetal, the 19-year-old sensation who is the reigning world champion and also the world number one, first combined with Toman Kumar to defend the mixed team gold against Indonesia's Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148. She then overcame a four-point deficit to defeat Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah 142-139 in a repeat of the Hangzhou 2023 individual final. The day started perfectly for India with Suvarna Raj taking the gold medal in women's F54 discus throw with a best effort of 15.66m. The wheelchair-bound 44-year-old delivered a consistent performance, recording four throws beyond the 15-metre to secure the biggest win of her career. Kapil Kumar and Swatik Patil also finished on the podium in their respective events, taking India's medal tally in swimming to nine. The 18-year-old visually impaired swimmer from Andhra Pradesh clocked 25.89 seconds to finish third in the 50m freestyle. He had earlier won silver medals in the men's S13 100m backstroke and 100m freestyle events..Asian Para Games 2026: How has India fared so far? articles.title: Asian Para Games: Thulasimathi clinches silver in women's singles SU5, remains in contention for two more golds
articles.summary: India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's
articles.body: India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. She will look to make amends in the remaining finals as India aim to add to their medal tally.Thulasimathi falls short against Yang after impressive semi-final comebackThulasimathi, currently ranked World No. 2, could not overcome Yang in the title clash, with the Chinese player securing the gold medal in straight games. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Two more gold medal opportunities awaitThulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high. She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Nitesh and Thulasimathi prevailed 21-19, 14-21, 21-17 to secure their place in the gold medal match.Later, Thulasimathi will team up with Manasi Girishchandra Joshi in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 final. The Indian pair will face China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian, giving Thulasimathi another opportunity to challenge for gold against the Chinese shuttler who defeated her in the singles final.Who is Thulasimathi Murugesan?Born on April 11, 2002, in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, Thulasimathi has established herself as one of India's leading para-badminton players. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. articles.title: Asian Para Games: Sandeep, Haney strike gold with world-record feats as India hit 100 medals
articles.summary: India's golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games gathered further momentum on Friday as Sandeep and Haney clinched gold medals with
articles.body: India's golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games gathered further momentum on Friday as Sandeep and Haney clinched gold medals with world-record performances in their respective events, taking the country's overall medal tally to 100. Sandeep set a new world record in the men's 400m T64, while Haney produced a record-breaking throw in the men's javelin F37/38 final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.Sandeep sets world record, Ajay Kumar claims bronzeSandeep clocked 52.28 seconds to win the men's 400m final, finishing comfortably ahead of Saudi Arabia's Nour Alsana, who secured silver in 53.13 seconds, a season's best. India's Ajay Kumar claimed bronze in 53.61 seconds, setting a Games record, while China's Huang Ruihua finished fourth with a personal-best time of 54.39 seconds.In the men's 400m, athletes from the T44 and T64 classifications competed together. While Sandeep and Alsana belong to the T44 category, Ajay Kumar competes in T64. Both classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments.Haney breaks world record with 60.49m javelin throwHaney followed with a world-record throw of 60.49 metres to claim gold in the men's javelin F37/38 event, earning 1,116 Raza points. Iran's Hormoz Seidikazpounji took silver with a personal-best throw of 50.68 metres, earning 1,009 points, while China's Yu Chengjie secured bronze with an Asian-record effort of 53.66 metres and 943 points.The combined F37 and F38 javelin categories are decided using Raza points, which account for the different classifications. This explains why Seidikazpounji finished ahead of Yu despite recording a shorter throw.India reach 100-medal milestoneThe double world-record triumph marked another significant milestone for India, whose overall medal tally crossed 100 at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: The next major WWE Premium Live Event will be Crown Jewel 2026. It has been scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. However, the country has been under constant air strikes by Yemen’s Houthis, putting the status of the event in serious question. During the conversation, the host asked him about WWE Crown Jewel’s status. He said that all their events are still set to go as planned. He said, “Right now, everything’s still set for this weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi. We have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November, a freeze art show, so, so far so good, nothing’s been canceled.”Furthermore, Emanuel also stated that one of their teams has been deployed to monitor the ongoing situation in Saudi Arabia daily. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this and kind of when and if it doesn’t happened where we can move it, it’s a daily monitoring”, said Emanuel.Have on-site promotions for WWE Crown Jewel 2026 begun in the city of Riyadh?On-site promotions for WWE Crown Jewel 2026 have begun in Riyadh. articles.title: My hard work paid off at the 2026 Asian Games: Suraj Kumar Chand
articles.summary: Written By: Harsh Kashiv Squash sensation Suraj Kumar Chand, who made India proud by winning a bronze medal at the 2026 Asian Games, recently visited
articles.body: Written By: Harsh KashivSquash sensation Suraj Kumar Chand, who made India proud by winning a bronze medal at the 2026 Asian Games, recently visited Ahmedabad for an event. Earlier this year, Chand scripted history by becoming the first Indian to win gold at the FISU World University Championship Squash. A video of him taking off his shirt in celebration after winning a thrilling final also went viral on Instagram. In a chat with us, the young athlete talks about his journey, future goals, and more.‘I have it in me to win more medals for India'Recalling his Asian Games experience, Chand says, “Winning an Asian Games medal was a long-term dream, and I really worked hard for it. The last two years were really tough, but after winning the medal, I felt that all the hard work paid off. After the Asian Games, I feel even more motivated. I believe I have it in me to win more medals for India, perhaps silver or gold next time.”With several tournaments lined up, Suraj is already back to training. He adds, “Hopefully, I can make it to the Olympics or win a gold medal at the Asian or Commonwealth Games. The Commonwealth Games will be held in Ahmedabad in 2030, and I hope to win a medal there.”‘Qualifying for the Olympics will be a big deal’With squash set to make its Olympic debut at the 2028 Olympics, Chand says, “The qualification criteria are very difficult. You have to maintain your ranking and be among the top 20 or top 16 players in the world. I still have a year or more, and there might also be a qualifying event starting in 2027. I am training for that and will try my best to make it. If I get into the Olympics, that will be a big deal for me."Talking about the 2030 Commonwealth Games, he adds, “Squash has been part of the Commonwealth Games for a long time, and it is a very important sport for India. We have won medals in squash. This time, with the CWG happening in Ahmedabad, more people will be able to watch us and there will be greater home support. I think we can win more medals. Hopefully, I will be part of the team and win a medal for India."'More people in India know about squash now'Chand believes squash still has considerable ground to cover in India. “There is still a big gap between squash and cricket in India. But since squash has been included in the Olympics, more people know about the game now. Anahat Singh won the World Junior Championships this year, and I won the World University Championship, becoming the first Indian to do so. After these two big wins, more people in India know about squash and are supporting it. More viewership means more support,” he says.He adds, “I think the game will improve in India. More people will start playing and more will participate at the grassroots level. We need to develop the game in schools and colleges. For instance, Egypt has the game at every level, with more than 200 players in every category. Right now, India is nowhere close to them, but we are getting there. That is a good sign, and I look forward to seeing us develop good players like Egypt."‘Gujarat's sports infrastructure is really good’Chand, who has visited Gujarat a couple of times for tournaments, feels, "If you compare the infrastructure with what we had five years ago, it is really good now. The setup here during the National Games was very good. Gujarat has excellent infrastructure and can host big tournaments. I can see squash becoming a big thing in Gujarat over the next two to three years."He has also observed a shift in the ambitions of young players. “When I was a junior, very few children wanted to play professionally or enter the professional circuit. Now, under-17 and under-19 players are entering the professional squash circuit and competing in PSA (Professional Squash Association) tournaments. That is a big difference,” he says.‘I watch Bhaag Milkha Bhaag for motivation’Away from the court, Chand keeps his routine simple. Despite the demands of training, travelling and competing on the international circuit, he prefers spending his free time with his family. He says, “Whenever I need some motivation, I watch Bhaag Milkha Bhaag. It is my favourite movie. I can watch it a thousand times. I follow Virat Kohli a lot. His discipline, both on and off the field, has motivated me a lot."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Arizona soccer suffers worst loss of season against Colorado
articles.summary: Head coach Becca Moros is looking inward after the 4-0 defeat
articles.body:
The Colorado Buffaloes have had some difficulty since they got into conference play, but there's a reason they came into Thursday night's game at Arizona with a top 10 RPI. The Buffaloes were 3-4 against the RPI top 25 and showed how they accomplished that with a 4-0 drubbing of the Wildcats at Mulcahy Stadium.

"We haven't given up that many goals all season, and I think what is most disappointing is not necessarily the loss, but that we didn't match up well," Arizona head coach Becca Moros said. "And I think that that's our fault. That's my fault…definitely disappointed in myself and our ability to compete at the level that we should have competed in that game."

Colorado had a nominal advantage in time of possession (52% to 48%), but it came down to where it possessed the ball. Sixty-seven percent of the Buffs' possession was in its offensive half. A full 33 percent were in the attacking third. That led to a 13-5 advantage in shots and a 6-0 advantage in shots on goal.

Arizona had a difficult time advancing the ball beyond midfield. The Wildcats spent 60 percent of their possession time on the defensive side of the pitch.

"I thought we could have played that team well off the park in the middle of the field, and we didn't play to our strengths there," Moros said.

Even when they got the ball near the 18, the Wildcats were quickly on their heels far too often. Colorado was able to counter attack repeatedly by making quick passes up the field. Arizona got back on defense, but it cut into the Wildcats' ability to sustain their own attacking posture.

That defense has typically been a strong unit for UA this season, but it had an extremely difficult time against CU. The Wildcats surrendered the first goal in the 22nd minute on a penalty kick. As has been the case with the majority of Arizona's penalty kicks this season, it came on a hand ball in the box.

The official did not initially call the foul, and the TV replay showed Trinity Dorsey holding her arms close to her body. He waved his hands as if indicating play on, perhaps because Dorsey did not appear to be trying to handle the ball even if it hit her arm. Several different angles showed it bouncing off her torso then brushing her back elbow.

The teams continued playing for almost two full minutes before the whistle was blown for a video review of the play. The review then stretched on. It was the second of several lengthy reviews in the match.

After review, Colorado was awarded the penalty kick. It was the eighth PK attempt surrendered by Arizona this season and the third successful one by an opponent.

"I don't think the penalty kick helped the momentum," Moros said.

As Moros suggested, Arizona did not handle falling behind very well. Less than three minutes later, Michaela McGowan scored Colorado's second goal of the game. It came on two nice passes in the box that found McGowan with enough space to get the shot off easily.

The Buffaloes added on 10 minutes into the second half. This pass bounced off Jace Holley and landed at her feet. Arizona players thought she settled it with her arm, but the official indicated she used her torso. It was again a fairly easy shot once it settled.

"They just smash balls in the box," Moros said. "It's not like there was anything elegant or confusing about it. You know, they beat us on the second balls, and the only thing I can look at is how did we need to adjust our shape to be a little more dominant, either in possession or to have better numbers around the ball. But again, that's the same kind of goals they scored all season."

The final goal was the first of the season for Phoenix native Faith Leyba . It was set up when Arizona goalkeeper Laurynn Ziller saved a serve into the box but stepped out of bounds while holding the ball. What was almost an Arizona possession turned into another Colorado corner kick. The CU defender was in the right place for her first goal of the season on the corner.

Arizona has two practice days to recover for senior day. They will take on the No. 9 Baylor Bears on Sunday after honoring six seniors in a pregame ceremony. Moros is looking inward for the answers before that.

"We've got to prepare them better, and we're going to do a better job for Sunday's game, making sure that we have a better matchup than that," she said.

articles.title: Drops mar otherwise productive night for Colston Loveland
articles.summary: Despite a pair of bad drops, Colston Loveland still finished with 69 yards and a score in a Week 7 win over New England.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears TE Colston Loveland recorded seven receptions, 69 yards, and a touchdown against the New England Patriots in Week 7. He was targeted a game-high 12 times.

Why It Matters: Coming off his best game of the season (6-65-1), Loveland saw his numbers tick up on Thursday night with seven catches for 69 yards and a score. It wasn't all positives for the second-year tight end, though, as he had a couple of bad drops. Perhaps the biggest thing that happened, however, was the injury to Cole Kmet (knee), who was carted off with a knee injury. Based on post-game comments from Ben Johnson, this doesn't sound like another Caleb Williams situation where it's not as bad as initially thought. If Kmet is indeed lost for a significant chunk of time, Loveland's role could increase a bit. Bottom line, Loveland is finally starting to put together the kind of numbers that fantasy owners were expecting coming into 2026. He's back to being playable as a midrange TE1.

articles.title: Zach Ertz shares message for Commanders WR Terry McLaurin
articles.summary: Zach Ertz knows all about suffering a devastating knee injury. He shared some encouraging words for Terry McLaurin this week.
articles.body:
The 2025 season was a difficult one for the Washington Commanders . After coming off a 12-win season and the franchise's first appearance in the NFC Championship Game in 33 years, the Commanders were crushed by injuries. Quarterback Jayden Daniels missed 10 games, wide receiver Terry McLaurin missed seven and tight end Zach Ertz suffered a devastating knee injury in Week 14.

Daniels and McLaurin returned in 2026, while Ertz last played in the burgundy and gold last December against the Vikings. Not wanting to end his career on that note, Ertz, 36, rehabbed and returned to the Philadelphia Eagles in September, where he spent the first 8.5 seasons of his NFL career.

Ertz spent the past two seasons with Washington, where he was one of Daniels' top two targets, alongside McLaurin. Ertz stayed close with his former Commanders teammates. When McLaurin suffered his own devastating knee injury in Monday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Ertz took to Instagram to show him some love.

Ertz and McLaurin were both leaders for the Commanders during their time together. While Ertz may have moved on to a division rival, he enjoyed his time in Washington, playing with guys like Daniels and McLaurin.

McLaurin was diagnosed with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee. It's a devastating injury, especially for a wide receiver who will turn 32 next season. While McLaurin is under contract with the Commanders next season, there's no more guaranteed money remaining, meaning they could move on from him with no penalty.

articles.title: Whither Vladimir? (Part 2)
articles.summary: On Tuesday, I looked at historical comps to Vladimir Guerrero jr.’s miserable 2026 season. The takeaway was that this kind of collapse is rare, occurring jus...
articles.body:
On Tuesday, I looked at historical comps to Vladimir Guerrero jr.'s miserable 2026 season. The takeaway was that this kind of collapse is rare, occurring just about 1% of the time for players under 30 who don't miss major time due to injury, that a lot of players who fall off a cliff like that never fully recover, but that Vlad's youth, health, and the fact that the drop almost all came from power issues rather than walks or strikeouts means he has better than average odds of recovering. Today, I want to dig a little bit into what actually drove his 2026 fall off.

The first thing to look at is whether there's a significant shift in how he was pitched. The graph below shows the pitch types he's seen by season in his career. The big thing to note is that over time he's seeing somewhat fewer four-seamers and steadily more sinkers, with the two pitches almost equal in 2026. That makes sense, as Vlad's weakness at the plate has always been the ability to elevate the ball. In his career, he has a -3 degree launch angle against sinkers compared to 14 degrees against four-seamers. He still hits sinkers very hard, but he struggles to elevate them enough to do damage.

I don't think pitch mix is a huge contributor to his 2026 struggles, though. For one, he has a .873 career OPS against sinkers, so while he's not as good against them as four-seamers it isn't as if they eat him up. For another, He hit the sinkers he saw this year pretty well (.849 OPS) but fell off against four seamers (.873, compared to .964 in his career).

The shift also doesn't look to be related to where pitchers attacked him. He actually saw more fastballs and off-speed pitches in the heart of the zone this season, compared to the last two:

Instead, I think the issue lies with his timing. Vlad swings extremely hard, and that didn't change this season. His 76.3mph average bat speed was in the 92nd percentile among qualified hitters, and while it was just slightly slower than 2025 it was significantly harder than 2023 or 2024. He has a relatively flat swing, with a 29 degree tilt that's 3 degrees below mlb average. That number was up one degree from 2024 and 2025, but the difference isn't substantial. His swing also didn't get any longer. All in all, it doesn't look like he changed his swing meaningfully this year.

What did change was the type of contact he made. Vlad didn't swing and miss more this season. In fact, his 82% contact rate was a career best and in the 73rd percentile in MLB, which is impressive for a player who swings as hard as he does. That contact wasn't nearly as good, though. The panel below shows an assortment of swing metrics, comparing his 24-25 results to this year. His bat speed is about the same, with a few less average swings and slightly more extremely hard ones. His attack angle, which is the angle the barrel of the bat is traveling when it hits the ball, shows a significant shift, though. He hit a lot more balls on the downswing and fewer in positive territory, especially the 0-10 degree range. He is attack direction, which measures the horizonal direction of the barrel at contact, shows that he went up the middle and slightly the other way less often, and pulled the ball a bit more. Relatedly, his contact depth shifted forward, meaning he was meeting the ball out in front of the plate more often. All these signs point to him being a little in front of or behind the pitch more often, and meeting it at the ideal point less. The last plot shows the result. Squared-up fraction is the percentage of the maximum possible exit velocity (based on how fast the bat and ball are moving) that the batter achieves. Anything over 80% is considered squared up, meaning the batter got most of the possible impact on the ball. Vlad's squared up fraction dropped in 2026, and the share of balls he really nailed, with 90% or better contact quality, fell dramatically.

The result of all those changes can be seen in the heatmap below. The black shape represents roughly the combinations of launch angle and exit velocity that StatCast considers barrels, the type of batted ball that accounts for most extra base hits. The blue inside the barrel zone and the red areas just below and to the left of it show that a lot of barrels from previous seasons were either hit hard but too low, in the -10 to 10 degree area, or were at the right angle but just a little too soft.

There's also a fair bit of red above +40 degrees and below -20 degrees. Those are angles that basically never result in useful contact. It looks like he maid more really bad contact than in past seasons, in addition to less really good contact.

My takeaway from all of this is that Vlad spent the whole season just a little off. His bat speed shows that he didn't lose raw strength, and there's nothing to suggest that his mechanics changed dramatically. He was just missing by a little bit, consistently. It's surprising to have such a dramatic effect and not be able to isolate a dramatic cause, but there's really no huge smoking gun here. It makes me wonder whether his vision really was an issue, or whether one of his nagging injuries was altering his swing just slightly, not in a way that shows up clearly in the metrics but enough to keep him from ever quite locking in.

In terms of his prognosis, I think this has to be seen as good news. If he'd lost his eye, or his bat speed, or his ability to get the bat on the ball, we'd have reason to worry that his skills had eroded in a way that wasn't going to come back. I don't see evidence for that, though. On the other hand, there's no obvious fix, either. There's no obvious adjustment to undo, or tweak that will address a revealed weakness. He just has to get right. Whether the coaching staff can help him do that this winter is maybe the single most important question facing the Blue Jays' long term future right now.

articles.title: Otro título mundial para Euskadi en pelota antes de jugar cuatro finales frente España
articles.standfirst: Edorta de Anta y Germán Elkoro ganan la final de parapelota. Este viernes habrá duelo vasco-español en las finales de mano individual, mano parejas, cesta punta femenina y paleta goma femenina.
articles.summary: Edorta de Anta y Germán Elkoro ganan la final de parapelota. Este viernes habrá duelo vasco-español en las finales de mano individual, mano parejas, cesta punta femenina y paleta goma femenina.
articles.body: España y Euskadi se enfrentarán este viernes en cuatro finales del Mundial de Pelota que se celebra en Buenos Aires. La entrada de la Federación Vasca como miembro de pleno derecho de la Federación Internacional da lugar a estos duelos que siguen la estela del partido por el oro en la cesta punta femenina (frontón 54 metros), en el que las representantes españolas Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi se impusieron a las vascas Maite Ortiz de Mendívil y Maia Goikoetxea. Las finales en las que habrá duelo entre españoles y vascos serán la de mano individual, mano parejas, cesta punta individual femenina y paleta goma femenina (30 metros). Además, este sábado ya hay seguro otro España-Euskadi en pala corta, un duelo que reedita el disputado en la fase de grupos. En esa ocasión los pelotaris vascos Esteban Gaubeka e Imanol Ibáñez vencieron a Carlos Baeza y Javier Insausti (15-10, 9-15 y 10-8). Hasta el momento, la selección vasca ha conseguido meterse en 12 de las 15 finales de las disciplinas en las que está presente en este Mundial. Este jueves Euskadi logró su segundo título mundialista. En esta ocasión en parapelota. Edorta de Anta y Germán Elkoro vencieron a los franceses Navarro y Cabanne por 15-10 y 15-9. La jornada se vio afectada por la lluvia y un 90% de humedad que obligó a suspender algunos partidos y reprogramarlos para este viernes. La final de mano por parejas entre los españoles Luis Sánchez e Íker Espinal y los franceses Peio Larralde y Andoni Iphar se vio afectada cuando ya estaba en juego. Aunque el trinquete es un escenario cubierto, el encuentro se paralizó con 7-3 arriba para España al estar el suelo mojado por la elevada humedad reinante en el exterior. La suspensión provocó también la reprogramación para este viernes de dos finales con presencia de España: la de xare ante Francia y la de paleta cuero ante Argentina. Quien sí pudo jugar antes su final individual fue Luis Sánchez ante el francés Ducassou. El galo se proclamó campeón del mundo al ganar por 15-7 y 15-12.

articles.title: Hamilton calls for Palestine and DR Congo freedom as Rwanda takes F1 spotlight
articles.summary: Rwanda’s controversial Formula One GP leads Lewis Hamilton to call for freedom for DR Congo, while renewing Palestine plea.
articles.body:
Seven-time Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton has renewed his call for freedom for Palestine when pressed on the controversial decision to award a Grand Prix to Rwanda.

The 41-year-old is the only Black competitor in the motorsport and said an African race would make people more aware of the continent, but recognised there were concerns and used the issue to expand on his stance on humanitarian issues across the world.

Human rights campaigners Amnesty International recently accused Formula One of hollow words and offering Rwanda a “sportswashing prize” – an accusation levelled at countries perceived to be using sport to improve a tarnished image abroad.

Hamilton, who was speaking before Sunday’s US Grand Prix, has long called for a Gaza ceasefire amid Israel’s genocidal war and returned to the matter – as well as other conflicts – when asked about a Grand Prix in Rwanda.

“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine,” Hamilton said.

“There’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage.”

Rwanda in the spotlight after Formula One GP award

Rwanda President Paul Kagame has been accused of repressive methods to keep his grip on power, with opponents dying in prisons, independent media muzzled, and other abuses.

Neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) joined the criticism of Formula One’s decision to award a race to Rwanda, which is accused by the DRC, the United States and United Nations experts of backing the M23 rebels fighting in the DRC.

“Of course, I don’t get to choose where we go,” Hamilton continued.

“Naturally, there are problems all over the world today, so I’ve seen many of the stories. But I think we really have to approach it with humility.

“Of course, going there doesn’t mean that you neglect the things that are happening there.

“So hopefully many people start to educate themselves a little bit more about what is happening there and what has happened there for hundreds of years. I hope that does spark the conversation.

“Growing up in England, they never taught us anything about Africa. It needs to be on the curriculum.

“A lot of the problems they have there are still results of colonialism and the West intervening.”

Formula One’s return to Africa has been Hamilton’s dream

Hamilton said a race in Africa was a dream that could keep him going longer in the sport now that Formula One has done a deal with Rwanda for a Grand Prix in the early 2030s .

The Ferrari driver will be 42 in January and has a contract for 2027. Fernando Alonso, the oldest active F1 driver, is 45 and recently signed up for another season with Aston Martin.

“I’m now forced to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa, and that’s been my dream, to be able to race in Africa,” Hamilton said on Thursday in a news conference alongside championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

“I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”

Antonelli, who replaced Hamilton at Mercedes last season and is still only 20 years old, encouraged him: “You got to do at least the first one.”

Hamilton, the sport’s first and only Black champion, has long campaigned for a race in Africa – a continent that last hosted a race at South Africa’s Kyalami circuit in 1993 – and spoke of his efforts.

“Countless meetings with the stakeholders, so many meetings with (F1 CEO) Stefano (Domenicali) at his office in London, but also on race weekends, countless calls: ‘What’s happening? Where are we going? Who are you meeting with?’

“Many meetings with different presidents from different countries. Lots of phone calls with different presidents from different countries within Africa,” he recalled.

“I think for me, it’s a place that deserves to have a Grand Prix. It’s about more than just one country. It’s about the continent itself.”

articles.title: Three medals in a day! Thulasimathi Murugesan caps Asian Para Games campaign with gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, Naveen strike gold for IndiaNitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Making his Asian Para Games debut, Naveen completed the win in 36 minutes.Pramod had to settle for silver after winning gold in the 2018 and 2022 editions. India's Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan also claimed silver in the women's singles SH6 final after losing to China's Li Fengmei.India close in on best-ever medal tallyIndia continued to collect medals across disciplines on Friday. Para shooter Mona Agarwal won her second gold of the Games in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final, setting a world record with 357.5 points. She finished 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang.In para archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men's recurve doubles event. Sandeep claimed the men's 400m T64 title, while Haney won gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 event.India also added silver medals through Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan, Pooja Jatyan and Bhawna Choudhary in women's recurve doubles, Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46 and Nimisha Suresh in the women's long jump T47. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. articles.title: Daniel Pulvett, campeón de Europa de ajedrez para ciegos
articles.standfirst: Con 16 años consiguió el título de maestro internacional
articles.summary: Con 16 años consiguió el título de maestro internacional
articles.body: El ajedrecista con discapacidad visual, Daniel Eduardo Pulvett, se ha proclamado en Creta (Grecia) campeón de Europa de ajedrez para ciegos tras nueve días de competición. Pulvett, de 34 años, comenzó a perder la vista con doce debido a una retinosis pigmentaria, justo cuando empezaba a conocer el ajedrez gracias a su padre. Con 16 años consiguió el título de maestro internacional y ahora en Creta ha ido de menos a más en el torneo representando a la Federación Española de Deportes para Ciegos (FEDC). Tuvo un pequeño tropiezo en la segunda ronda haciendo tablas y después ganó cuatro partidas de manera consecutiva, de tal forma que consiguió mantener un punto de ventaja desde la ronda seis. A partir de ahí, fue administrando su ventaja con ese punto extra hasta que en su última partida, celebrada este jueves, firmó tablas para alzarse con el título de campeón continental por primera vez en su carrera deportiva. Tras conquistar el torneo, Pulvett se mostraba “súper contento por conseguir el objetivo de quedar campeón”. “Aunque sea un campeonato individual todo esto no sería posible sin el apoyo de mis compañeros de viaje”, dijo en referencia a los otros dos ajedrecistas españoles participantes, Alejandro Martínez (18º) y José Manuel Vela (20º clasificado), al entrenador Victoriano Gallego y al técnico de la FEDC, Pablo Martínez. “Victoriano y Pablo son como el motor del equipo porque hacen que todo funcione, que esté en su lugar, que preparemos las partidas, que tengamos los tableros, los relojes. El más mínimo detalle lo tenemos a disposición gracias a ellos”, señaló, sin olvidarse del apoyo de su familia, tanto desde Madrid como desde Venezuela, su país de nacimiento.

articles.title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Who is Himanshu Nandal?Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medalsNandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Rangers, the Maple Leafs and Other NHL Teams Whose 2026 Offseason Pickups Are Paying Off Early
articles.summary: On Oct. 20, we looked at five NHL teams already regretting their 2026 offseason moves. Now, we're looking at those whose offseason pickups are paying off thus far in 2026-27.
articles.body:
On Oct. 20, we looked at five NHL teams already regretting their 2026 offseason moves. Now, we're looking at those whose offseason pickups are paying off thus far in 2026-27.

Like the five teams whose moves haven't panned out so far, those on this list dipped into this summer's trade and free-agent markets to bolster their rosters. Some also made preseason moves to address their needs.

Of course, the season is still early. Some of these moves that look good now could become costly as the schedule progresses. Some acquisitions could become costly over time if injuries or age-related decline limit the players' contributions.

For now, however, the five clubs we're profiling here have done well thus far. Follow along as we examine their performance.

Notable offseason additions: Head coach Mike Babcock, goaltenders Devon Levi and Frederik Andersen, defensemen Shakir Mukhamadullin and Ryan Shea, and forwards Owen Michaels and Alex Formenton.

After back-to-back seasons as Stanley Cup finalists, the Edmonton Oilers were eliminated from the opening round of last spring's playoffs by the upstart Anaheim Ducks. That led to a coaching change and several roster changes.

The most notable move was hiring Mike Babcock as their new head coach. His appointment followed controversy surrounding his previous tenures with the Toronto Maple Leafs and Columbus Blue Jackets. Nevertheless, stars Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Zach Hyman supported his hiring .

So far, the Oilers have bought into Babcock's disciplined defense-first system. As of Oct. 22, they were second in the Western Conference with a 7-1-1 record. His system hasn't hampered their offensive game. McDavid, Draisaitl, and puck-moving defenseman Evan Bouchard are among the league's leading scorers.

Levi, meanwhile, is making the most of his opportunity with the Oilers after failing to crack the Buffalo Sabres' lineup. The 24-year-old goaltender was 5-1-0 in his six starts with a 2.83 goals-against average. He's looking more comfortable with each start.

Michaels, 24, was an undrafted free agent who has put up solid defensive stats on the third line as the Oilers' only right-handed center. Meanwhile, the 29-year-old Shea is logging big minutes as he settles into their second defensive pairing with Connor Murphy.

Mukhamadullin was acquired in the Darnell Nurse trade, but has been a frequent healthy scratch. Formenton has four points in nine games as a third-line winger. Andersen is still recovering from a knee injury suffered in the Stanley Cup Final and is expected to return in December .

Time will tell whether the Oilers can maintain their current pace and remain among the league's top teams, let alone return to the Stanley Cup Final. So far, however, it's tough to argue with their results, with several offseason additions making significant contributions.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Brady Tkachuk, Lars Eller, and Garnet Hathaway; defenseman Radko Gudas; and goaltender Jacob Markstrom.

The Florida Panthers made two of this offseason's most notable trades. On June 21, they acquired left wing Brady Tkachuk from the Ottawa Senators. Nine days later, they replaced departing starting goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky by dealing for Jacob Markstrom from the New Jersey Devils.

Landing Tkachuk was a major move, reuniting him with his older brother, Matthew. The 27-year-old left winger was scoreless in his first five games, but netted seven goals and 11 points in his next five contests, including back-to-back natural hat tricks, to sit second behind Matthew among the Panthers' scoring leaders.

Brady Tkachuk struggled early while he and his brother played on separate lines. As injuries mounted, head coach Paul Maurice paired them, and they've been on a tear since.

Markstrom, 36, had big skates to fill, replacing the popular Bobrovsky. Nevertheless, he sported a record of 3-1-1 in his first five games with a 2.21 goals-against average, including a season-opening shutout of the Carolina Hurricanes. He's currently sidelined for one to two weeks with an upper-body injury .

Eller was among the Panthers' notable depth signings this summer, joining Hathaway and Gudas. A versatile two-way forward who can play center or right wing, the 37-year-old is seeing second-line minutes with Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand sidelined. He's collected five assists in 10 games.

The Panthers missed the playoffs last season after winning back-to-back Stanley Cups. Their summer pickups could be contributing factors in the renewed pursuit of hockey's holy grail.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Pavel Dorofeyev, Eeli Tolvanen, and Oliver Bjorkstrand; defensemen Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson; goaltender Joonas Korpisalo.

After two years of retooling his roster, New York Rangers general manager Chris Drury continued adding pieces during this offseason. So far, most of those pickups have helped the Rangers contend with the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes for first place in the Metropolitan Division .

Durzi and Pettersson have provided much-needed depth to the Rangers' blue line as their second defense pairing . Both have logged over 20 minutes per game , including time on the penalty kill. They're also among the Blueshirts' leaders in blocked shots and takeaways.

Meanwhile, Tolvanen and Bjorkstrand bring experienced depth to their forward lines. The two-way Tolvanen is among their leaders in blocked shots and hits. The emergence of Tye Kartye has dropped Bjorkstrand to the fourth line, but he's tied for second on the team with four goals.

Dorofeyev was Drury's biggest addition, acquired from the Vegas Golden Knights and signed to a seven-year, $77 million contract. He's struggled in the early going with five points in 11 games, but it should be a matter of time before he finds his groove with his new club.

Korpisalo was acquired from the Boston Bruins. The 32-year-old netminder is sidelined by a lower-body injury and is expected to remain out until mid-November, but he could provide veteran experience for young Dylan Garand, who's been thrust into the starter's job following Igor Shesterkin's season-ending injury.

So far, the Rangers have benefited from most of these pickups. Some have already contributed to their early success, while others could play key roles going forward once they adjust to their new surroundings and return from injury.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Kirill Marchenko, Gavin McKenna, Jack Roslovic and Nick Paul; defenseman Darren Raddysh; and goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky.

The Toronto Maple Leafs were among the busiest teams during the offseason. They not only made several significant roster changes but also overhauled their management and coaching staff. New general manager John Chayka proved willing to make some bold moves to upgrade his new club's roster.

All eyes are on Marchenko and McKenna. Marchenko, 27, was acquired in a blockbuster multi-player trade that sent popular winger Matthew Knies to the Columbus Blue Jackets, while the 18-year-old McKenna was the first overall pick in this year's draft.

Marchenko has adjusted well so far. He has 11 points in as many games, including a hat trick against the Buffalo Sabres on Oct. 15. McKenna is still learning the ropes at the NHL level, but has six points in 11 games and seems more comfortable with each game.

Roslovic is a streaky scorer but has nine points in his first 10 games. Meanwhile, Paul has moved up from being a checking-line center to replace the sidelined John Tavares on the second line. He is showing promising signs of bouncing back from last season's injury-hampered performance with the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Not every acquisition has panned out thus far. Bobrovsky has been inconsistent between the pipes, and Raddysh hasn't regained his 70-point form from last season with the Lightning.

Nevertheless, most of the Maple Leafs' offseason additions have helped them get off to a good start. There are still issues to be sorted out (especially defensively), but if Bobrovsky and Raddysh regain their form and Roslovic and Paul become consistent contributors, the Leafs should return to the postseason.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Alex Tuch, Boone Jenner, and Jordan Kyrou, and defenseman Vincent Desharnais.

After finishing atop the Eastern Conference in 2024-25, the Washington Capitals failed to make the playoffs last season. General manager Chris Patrick wasted no time addressing that issue, acquiring Tuch and Kyrou through trades with Buffalo and St. Louis and signing free agents Jenner and Desharnais.

With a record of 5-4-0 after nine games, the Capitals are off to a decent start thus far, partly because of their offseason acquisitions.

Tuch, who signed an eight-year contract with the Capitals, is one of their leading scorers with five goals and seven points. The 30-year-old power forward has adjusted well thus far with his new teammates on the top line .

Jenner, 33, has adjusted well to his new team after 13 seasons with the Columbus Blue Jackets. He's centering the second line and sits among their leading scorers with four goals and five points in nine games.

Kyrou needed a bit of time to adjust, but the speedy 28-year-old winger seems to be rounding into form with six points in nine games. Meanwhile, shutdown blueliner Desharnais is sixth among all NHL defensemen in plus/minus (plus-9), logging second-pairing minutes and leading the club with 22 hits.

The Capitals want to regain their 2024-25 form and stage a final Stanley Cup run for captain Alex Ovechkin before he retires at the end of this season. Tuch, Jenner, Kyrou, and Desharnais could play bigger roles with this club as it transitions toward the post-Ovechkin era.
