articles.title: Way-Too-Early Predictions For WWE WrestleMania 43 Match Card
articles.summary: Seeds are already being planted for WWE WrestleMania 43 and it's not even November yet.
articles.body:
Seeds are already being planted for WWE WrestleMania 43 and it's not even November yet.

Historically, however, it's in the final few months of the year that the company begins building toward the spring spectacle, or at least putting together preliminary plans for what the major matches will be.

There has been speculation about the top matches at WrestleMania 43 and whether WWE will bring back familiar faces for the event, which is currently scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia. However, appearances by legends such as The Rock and "Stone Cold" Steve Austin have not been confirmed.

WWE has more than enough star power on its active roster to fill out the two-night weekend and still have a handful of notable names left over. Of course, anything can change creatively between now and then, and there's no telling who could be sidelined with an injury.

These are the way-too-early match card predictions for WrestleMania 43.

World Heavyweight Championship: Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi

From the moment Oba Femi decisively defeated Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42, it was clear he was destined to win a world title sooner rather than later.

Realistically, he should have already challenged for and won the World Heavyweight Championship by now (specifically at SummerSlam following his King of the Ring victory that earned him a title shot), but all signs point to WWE holding off on him having his crowning moment at WrestleMania 43.

That would explain why Reigns has had a stranglehold on the prestigious prize since 'Mania back in April and will likely continue to reign as champ through the spring spectacle. Femi has repeatedly called out Reigns on post-show panels but has yet to cross paths with him on WWE TV.

When they do finally go face-to-face, it will be a massive deal.

WWE is attempting to keep Femi busy with random obstacles such as Lesnar and The Vision in the meantime. Expect Femi to win the men's Royal Rumble (the exact match where he made his main roster debut earlier this year) and set his sights on The Tribal Chief from there.

Royce Keys should undoubtedly challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship at some point in the coming months given the ongoing faction warfare with The Bloodline and The 946, but he won't walk into WrestleMania 43 with the title.

That leaves him without an obvious opponent at the event, and the same can be said for all of The Vision. They've been at odds with Oba Femi as of late but are virtually guaranteed to come out on the losing end of that feud.

Ideally, Bron Breakker would be in a marquee match at 'Mania next April, especially after missing this past year's installment due to injury (that was where he returned but didn't wrestle), but similar to Keys, there isn't one match that's a "must" for him to have unless he jumps ship to SmackDown or leaves The Vision.

WWE has previously used multi-person tag team matches at WrestleMania to get wrestlers without clear storylines onto the card. That could be the case for The Vision and The 946.

If built up properly, this could be a fun brawl and a solid showcase for everyone involved. A Street Fight stipulation would make for the most exciting scenario and allow them to go all out.

Women's World Championship: Liv Morgan vs. Roxanne Perez

WWE shouldn't be waiting so long to get to the big blow-up between Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez, but as things stand, that appears to be the most likely Women's World Championship match for WrestleMania 43.

Morgan recently regained the gold at Money in the Bank but has no challengers waiting in the wings. Her rivalries with Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch have been done to death and no one on the Raw roster has enough momentum to feel like a legitimate threat to the title.

WWE's primary goal going forward should be to tease tension between Morgan and Perez so fans will rally behind The Prodigy and want to see her dethrone the champion. If WWE books this bout before WrestleMania, any other matchup for Morgan at the event would pale in comparison.

This is the strongest story WWE could possibly tell with the women of the red brand en route to The Show of Shows.

Perez has had so many stellar showings in the women's Royal Rumble over the years that her being the one to win this upcoming installment would be a perfect way to put this program into motion.

Changes WWE Needs for WrestleMania 43 🛠️

Kevin Owens and Randy Orton were scheduled to face off in a potential show-stealer at WrestleMania 41, but the match was canceled after KO announced that he needed neck surgery.

Orton instead faced Joe Hendry, who answered his open challenge at the event, while Owens remained sidelined until his return at SummerSlam 2026.

The two have interacted on a number of occasions since Owens has been back on the blue brand, but despite Owens being responsible for putting The Viper on the shelf two years ago, there's barely been any animosity between the two.

That's likely due to Owens' focus being firmly on the Undisputed WWE Championship and Orton targeting Cody Rhodes, but come WrestleMania 43, they should rekindle their rivalry and settle their score once and for all.

Even with the roles reversed, there's enough bad blood from Owens and Orton's past to make this match worthy of the WrestleMania stage. The endgame of their original feud was supposed to see Orton punt Owens in the head, and there's no reason for the story of their rematch to be drastically different.

Both men deserve a significant singles match at 'Mania, and considering they've already worked with almost everyone else on the SmackDown roster, giving them a chance to have the WrestleMania payoff they were previously deprived of would be the best use of them.

WWE Women's Championship: Tiffany Stratton vs. Rhea Ripley

Tiffany Stratton winning the women's Money in the Bank ladder match made it clear that her friendship with Chelsea Green isn't going to last much longer, and that the WWE Women's Championship will soon be back in her possession.

Stratton vs. Green isn't and shouldn't be the WrestleMania match, either. Rather, it's a fine feud to fill the gap between now and then ahead of Rhea Ripley's return to the ring.

Stratton unsuccessfully cashing in her contract and subsequently turning heel out of frustration would pack more of a punch than simply cashing in on Green and winning the title.

Stratton and Green could then have a series of matches over the next few months, culminating in The Center of the Universe regaining the championship. From there, Ripley would be her biggest possible WrestleMania opponent.

Ripley vs. Stratton has happened before, but never as a full-fledged rivalry, and the dynamic between them would make for must-see television. Of course, the story writes itself with Ripley never being beaten for the belt before she had to vacate it over the summer.

The Eradicator's constant involvement in the championship picture risks becoming repetitive. However, her star power and the fresh matchups still available make it easy to see why she would be integral to next year's WrestleMania plans.

LA Knight's immediate future in WWE remains uncertain following his loss to Roman Reigns at Money in the Bank. He fell short when it mattered most yet again and hasn't given a clear indication of what he intends to do next.

The only answer to his recent woes would be to turn heel, or at least lean more into being an aggressive loner character.

That means severing ties with Solo Sikoa, who has since made amends with The Bloodline. That's sure to irritate Knight, leading to The Megastar in turn forming a temporary alliance with The 946 for WarGames at Survivor Series.

Of all the popular babyfaces Knight could feud with for WrestleMania season, Seth Rollins leads the list of most intriguing options, if only because they've only scratched the surface of what they can do together and have proven to have quality chemistry in the ring.

Rollins is stuck in a similar position at the moment in that he doesn't have a clear direction post-Roman Reigns, but Knight would be a fantastic foil for him heading into The Show of Shows. It'd also get Knight back in a prominent spot at WrestleMania and ensure he doesn't go right back to pulling midcard duty.

Undisputed WWE Championship: Cody Rhodes vs. CM Punk

The Undisputed WWE Championship scene on SmackDown is in such a state of flux these days that it's impossible to predict what the exact title match will be for WrestleMania 43, but CM Punk and Cody Rhodes running it back for the coveted title seems to be a safe bet.

It was considered a dream match when they first waged war with the gold up for grabs at SummerSlam. It was a good but not great match, which left fans wondering whether they were intentionally holding back for a better bout down the road.

That was the same show where Randy Orton returned to cost Cody the title, so Punk's victory was tainted. A WrestleMania rematch would afford them the opportunity to have the barn burner they're capable of, and deliver more captivating promos leading into the event if one of them were to go heel beforehand.

It's essentially the same formula Rhodes' last two WrestleMania rivalries with John Cena and Orton followed, but here, The American Nightmare can be the one to turn heel and embrace the boos he's been receiving on and off for the last little while.

Some fans have been clamoring for heel Rhodes, and Punk might be the best possible person for him to get heat for betraying.

It's a match that's been done before, but no other combination of current SmackDown stars would make as much sense.

There's plenty more that can be explored with Punk and Rhodes, and while WWE should be putting newer names in these spots, the event emanating from Saudi Arabia is bound to push them toward going with the tried and true and booking main events with established acts like these two.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Ranking WWE and AEW's Hottest Storylines From Roman Reigns vs. 946, Sami Zayn to New Level's Rise
articles.summary: Professional wrestling is often at its best when it rewards our knowledge of the genre. Some of the best storylines pay off years of continuity or offer a wink and a nod to real-life occurrences.
articles.body:
Professional wrestling is often at its best when it rewards our knowledge of the genre. Some of the best storylines pay off years of continuity or offer a wink and a nod to real-life occurrences.

Let's face it. Many of us watch a lot of wrestling, and we can't wait to tell anyone who will listen how much we know about our favorite pastime. Some of the best characters know how to break the fourth wall and appeal to savvy fans for the maximum reaction.

That's what makes someone like Kevin Owens so relatable or adds background to a rivalry years in the making. It makes us want to discover more about our favorite wrestlers and be a part of the communal experience.

With that in mind, these are the hottest storylines in WWE and All Elite Wrestling right now.

Jay White's shocking heel turn was the reset that AEW Dynamite needed following WrestleDream.

The Bang Bang Gang has been wildly popular since the New Zealand wrestler returned at Forbidden Door. However, the stable has lacked a clear direction for months, and White has struggled to regain momentum as a singles competitor.

The Death Riders have received strong crowd support in the weeks following PAC's death and AEW's tribute show. The Bang Bang Gang's new alliance with The Dogs gives Jon Moxley's group a compelling opposing faction.

This also gives David Finlay and Clark Connors something interesting to do and makes Gabe Kidd an exclusive member of The Death Riders. The trio had been floundering, and Kidd fits much better with Mox and his pupils.

There's so much potential here. Finlay has a long history with White dating back to their time with New Japan Pro-Wrestling, and their Bullet Club lore could eventually lead to a conflict with The Elite.

Kevin Owens vs. CM Punk has been one of the most entertaining WWE feuds of 2026.

The company capitalized on Owens' long-awaited return at SummerSlam and pivoted to the matchup fans have clamored for since 2023.

Twenty years of pent-up animosity between the two set the stage for memorable segments that masterfully blurred the lines between fiction and reality.

This entry would rank higher, but the rivalry has cooled off a little since their Undisputed WWE Championship match and the build to Money in the Bank. Nevertheless, it's still an integral part of SmackDown's world title scene that will likely culminate in a Triple Threat match with Sami Zayn.

Most weeks, their interactions are the best thing on the blue brand. There's still plenty of interest in another one-on-one match or a long-overdue Owens world title run.

On the latest episode of Raw, Sami Zayn finally confronted Roman Reigns as the undisputed WWE champion.

"The Honorary Uce" has been linked to The Tribal Chief and The Bloodline since 2022. As such, many fans were disappointed when they never crossed paths after Zayn's first WWE title win at Night of Champions.

Fortunately, their upcoming match at Crown Jewel offers a rewarding new chapter to their turbulent friendship. This time, the dynamic has flipped because the Canadian star has carved his own lane as a heel champion, and Reigns refuses to acknowledge his accomplishments.

Zayn has been on fire on the microphone since he regained the title, and he held his own in their first war of words. Still, The OTC got the last word in a segment that perfectly encapsulated their history together and promoted their rematch for the Men's Crown Jewel Championship.

Way-Too-Early WrestleMania 43 Predictions 🔮

Changes WWE Needs for WrestleMania 43 🛠️

Latest Rumors Around Wrestling Universe 👊

2. Swerve Strickland and The New Level vs. The Good, The Bad and The Ugly

The AEW trios division has surprisingly produced the company's best storyline at the moment.

Swerve Strickland and The New Level have been an excellent fit. The change of scenery has reinvigorated Kofi and Austin Creed, and their reactions to revelations about Strickland's past are legitimately funny.

More to the point, their feud with The Good, The Bad and The Ugly produced the best match at All Out and a standout 2-out-of-3-Falls bout at WrestleDream. Strickland's exchanges with "Hangman" Adam Page have been electric. It has also been a blast to watch Kofi and Creed reluctantly participate in their all-consuming, bitter rivalry.

To that end, the 36-year-old just challenged Page to a Texas Death match at Full Gear for the trios title. We can only imagine how far Strickland will go to get Hangman to accept his challenge and how the two could top their previous encounter under that stipulation.

Can Strickland's alliance with The New Level and Page's partnership with Brodido survive another descent into their bitter rivalry? That's the real question.

1. Roman Reigns and The Bloodline vs. The 946

The 946 has become a convincing threat to The Bloodline ahead of Survivor Series: WarGames.

Royce Keys has exceeded expectations as the leader of the crew, and Carmelo Hayes is a welcome addition. Their placement in the main event segments on Raw is a refreshing change of pace and a great way to build anticipation for the men's WarGames match.

WWE's annual tradition has lost some of its luster, but it's fun to see some new faces benefit during the lead-in. It's also interesting to see The Bloodline under pressure for a change. No one has caught them slipping like this since the group's inception.

Reigns' appearance on the latest episode of Raw elevated the dynamic as the two factions finally shared the ring. We can't wait to see how Jacob Fatu's return in the coming weeks adds to the rivalry.

articles.title: What does Connor Hellebuyck’s suspension update mean for the Winnipeg Jets and their NHL trade plans before the Heritage Classic
articles.summary: The Winnipeg Jets are considering delaying Connor Hellebuyck's return-related physical after his suspension expires on October 23, impacting trade negotiations and team dynamics before the Heritage Classic against the Montreal Canadiens.
articles.body: The Winnipeg Jets could delay Connor Hellebuyck’s return-related physical until after the Heritage Classic, according to a report citing TSN insider Darren Dreger. The development comes as the star goaltender’s team-imposed suspension is scheduled to expire Friday, October 23, two days before Winnipeg faces the Montreal Canadiens in the outdoor NHL event.The reported possibility does not confirm that Hellebuyck will return to the lineup or that a trade is imminent. Winnipeg is still exploring options after the three-time Vezina Trophy winner requested a trade during the offseason. The timing also places the franchise under pressure to manage the unresolved situation without allowing it to overshadow one of the biggest events on its schedule.Why NHL star Connor Hellebuyck and the Winnipeg Jets face uncertaintyDarren Dreger’s latest report suggests the Winnipeg Jets and Connor Hellebuyck could agree to postpone the physical process until after the Heritage Classic. The idea would allow the team to focus on its outdoor game while discussions about the goaltender’s future continue in the background. However, the reported understanding has not been confirmed as a formal agreement by the Jets or Hellebuyck.The distinction matters because the end of a suspension does not automatically guarantee an immediate return to the lineup. Winnipeg would still need to determine the next steps in a situation involving the player’s trade request, his absence from training camp and the club’s plans for its goaltending position.Why is Connor Hellebuyck’s suspension ending?Connor Hellebuyck’s suspension stems from his failure to report to the Winnipeg Jets’ training camp after requesting a trade. He publicly confirmed on August 27 that he had asked to leave Winnipeg earlier in the offseason, saying that moving on was the best path forward for him and his family. The Jets suspended him after he failed to report when camp opened in September.Sportsnet insider Elliotte Friedman previously reported that the suspension was scheduled to end October 23. The relevant provision of the NHL’s collective bargaining agreement allows a club to impose a disciplinary suspension of reasonable length when a player returns after an unauthorized absence from training camp. The reported expiry date therefore creates a decision point for Winnipeg, rather than guaranteeing that Hellebuyck will immediately rejoin the team.How could the Heritage Classic affect the Jets’ plans?The Winnipeg Jets are scheduled to face the Montreal Canadiens in the Heritage Classic on Sunday, October 25, at Princess Auto Stadium. With the suspension’s reported end date falling just two days before the outdoor game, a decision about Hellebuyck could attract considerable attention during the event’s buildup.The Jets have also had to manage their goaltending without their established starter. NHL.com reported that Winnipeg could consider several paths, including a trade, keeping Hellebuyck away from the team or bringing him back into the organization. Head coach Scott Arniel previously said the situation remained uncertain and that the next move would depend on how events unfolded.Why do NHL trade rumors around Connor Hellebuyck continue?The central issue remains Hellebuyck’s desire to leave Winnipeg. Reuters reported on October 20 that at least three teams were involved in trade discussions, although a deal before the suspension expired was not guaranteed. Hellebuyck’s full no-movement clause gives him significant influence over a potential destination, complicating negotiations for the Jets.What happens next? The Heritage Classic could take place without a resolution to the dispute. Unless the Winnipeg Jets or Hellebuyck confirm a change, the reported possibility of delaying the physical should be treated as an update on the negotiations; not confirmation of a trade, a return or a breakthrough between the two sides.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: CAS clears Japan’s Olympic silver medallist Ikeda of doping, overturns ban
articles.summary: Race walker Koki Ikeda returns to competition immediately; Ethiopia’s marathon runner Ruti Aga given 6-year doping ban.
articles.body:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld an appeal by Japanese race walker Koki Ikeda against World Athletics, clearing the Tokyo Olympic silver medallist of an anti-doping rule violation and making him immediately eligible to compete again.

The 28-year-old was provisionally suspended in November 2024 before receiving a four-year sanction from the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) in February 2025 for allegedly using or attempting to use a banned drug.

Ikeda was not allowed to participate in the Japan Race Walking Championships in February 2025, and all his competitive results between June 20, 2023 and November 1, 2024 were disqualified.

Ikeda challenged the ruling at CAS in March 2025, rejecting the doping allegations brought by World Athletics, which had alleged blood manipulation based on abnormalities in his Athlete Biological Passport.

The case was heard by a CAS panel in Lausanne in May. While the panel accepted that several readings in Ikeda’s biological profile were abnormal, it found there was a reasonable non-doping explanation for the findings.

CAS said Ikeda supported his case with substantial medical and expert evidence, providing a broader factual basis than was available during the proceedings before the World Athletics tribunal.

The appeal body overturned the four-year sanction, concluding that the anti-doping charge had not been established and that no ban should apply.

Ikeda placed second in the 20km event at the Tokyo Games as well as at the World Championships in Eugene in 2022. He finished seventh at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Ethiopia’s Aga handed six-year doping ban

Ethiopian marathon runner Ruti Aga, winner of the 2019 Tokyo Marathon, was given a six-year ban for the presence or use of the prohibited substance methylprednisolone and tampering with evidence, the AIU said on Thursday.

The AIU said Aga, 32, received a two-year ban after testing positive for methylprednisolone, a prohibited steroid that can reduce pain and fatigue and aid recovery, after winning a half marathon in China in March.

It added four years to the ban after finding she had misled investigators during an interview and submitted a fake prescription to justify her use of the substance.

Aga has been provisionally suspended since September 10, with the ban running from that date.

She has finished second three times and third twice at World Marathon Majors.

His right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm in Himachal Pradesh when he was six years old. He went on to establish himself as one of India's leading para-athletes, particularly in the high jump.With two gold medals apiece, Mona and Nishad will lead India's contingent at Saturday's closing ceremony, providing a fitting conclusion to their impressive campaigns in Aichi-Nagoya.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why do the Detroit Red Wings want a “home run” return for Dylan Larkin despite multiple NHL offers deemed fair
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings aim for a blockbuster trade return for Dylan Larkin, despite several fair offers, as they seek immediate talent and future assets.
articles.body: The Detroit Red Wings are reportedly holding out for a major return for Dylan Larkin despite receiving multiple offers described as fair. NHL insider Nick Kypreos reported that Detroit is seeking a “triple, if not a home run,” suggesting the organization wants a package that exceeds a standard market-value return for its captain.The situation puts Detroit’s trade strategy under scrutiny. Larkin remains an experienced center and a key figure for the franchise, but any potential move depends on whether an interested team can meet the Red Wings’ demands and whether the captain is willing to approve the destination.Why Dylan Larkin and the Detroit Red Wings await NHL trade clarityNick Kypreos reported that the Detroit Red Wings have multiple offers for Larkin that are considered fair, but the team has not accepted one because it is waiting for a more substantial package. His description of the desired return as a “triple, if not a home run” signals that Detroit may be prioritizing an exceptional deal over a merely reasonable one.That distinction is important. An offer can be viewed as fair without providing the specific mix of immediate NHL talent and future assets that Detroit wants. Trading a captain is a significant roster decision, so the front office has reason to weigh both the player’s value and the long-term direction of the team.Which NHL teams could make a stronger offer?The Red Wings have more potential trade partners after Larkin reportedly expanded his list of acceptable destinations from three teams to 10. The list includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. The Montreal Canadiens are not included, despite fan interest in bringing Larkin to Montreal.Minnesota and Vegas remain notable possibilities because they were among Larkin’s original preferred destinations. However, an interested team must balance the cost of acquiring him with its salary-cap position and the players it would need to surrender. Detroit reportedly wants established players who can contribute immediately, rather than a package made up mainly of draft picks and prospects.How does Dylan Larkin’s contract affect trade talks?Larkin’s contract is another major consideration. He is signed through the 2030-31 season on an eight-year, $69.6 million deal, carrying an average annual salary-cap hit of $8.7 million. His full no-trade clause also means Detroit cannot simply send him to whichever team offers the largest package. Any move must account for his approved destinations and the financial realities facing potential buyers.That combination gives Larkin meaningful control over the process while placing pressure on the Red Wings to negotiate carefully. Expanding his list creates more possibilities, but it does not guarantee that any of the 10 teams can meet Detroit’s preferred price.What happens next for the Detroit Red Wings?The immediate question is whether interim general manager Shawn Horcoff can secure the type of return the organization wants. If another team improves its proposal with NHL-ready talent and future assets, the Red Wings could have a stronger reason to move forward. If not, the club may continue weighing its options rather than accepting an offer it considers insufficient.For now, the reported offers do not confirm that a trade is imminent. Kypreos’ update points to a gap between what Detroit considers an acceptable return and the larger package it hopes to receive. The next significant development will depend on whether an interested team is willing and able to improve its offer, and whether the deal fits Larkin’s contractual protections.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dortmund to reward football supporters who don’t use phone during matches
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund’s new scheme does not mean a ban on supporters using their phones and system is voluntary for fans.
articles.body:
A stadium selfie could soon be to a fan’s detriment at German football giant Borussia Dortmund after the club announced plans to reward those who leave their phones alone during the game.

Dortmund is offering signed jerseys and gift cards for club merchandise to fans who use an app which measures how often they unlock their phones at its stadium.

Arguing that “more and more fans are annoyed by selfies, streaming, and social media in the stands,” Dortmund says supporters can volunteer to use a “fan mode” in the club’s app, starting Saturday with a home game against Eintracht Frankfurt.

Fan mode will measure how often the phone is unlocked during the game, not counting the halftime break, and award points to people based on how little they use the device, with prizes on offer for those with the most points. Each time the phone is unlocked, the user loses points.

“Over 81,000 people in the stadium, singing, cheering, and holding their breath together: this here and now is irreplaceable,” Dortmund CEO Carsten Cramer said in a statement late on Thursday.

The rewards scheme and app are voluntary, and there’s no ban on fans using their phones.

German football is famed for its vocal fanbase, especially Dortmund’s vast and loud “Yellow Wall” standing section.

The club’s stance is part of a backlash in German football against attempts to turn its stadium atmosphere into social media content, especially by influencers using professional camera equipment.

Second-division club Hertha Berlin said this month it was banning “commercially produced and monetised” video productions from its games, while allowing fans to take photos and videos for personal use.

Another club, Dynamo Dresden, said in August it would ban commercial filming for social media, saying it wanted to ensure fans felt comfortable at the game and to protect the club’s TV rights deals.

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweepThe 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Pranav Soorma defends club throw crownSoorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. articles.title: Steelers’ D.K. Metcalf Put on Notice Days Before Saints Matchup
articles.summary: NFL analyst Gregg Rosenthal argued Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf is no longer the team's top wideout entering Week 7. The post Steelers’ D.K...
articles.body:
Veteran wide receiver D.K. Metcalf turned in one of his better games of the young 2026 season in the Pittsburgh Steelers comeback victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Metcalf hauled in a season-high 11 catches for 93 yards.

The Steelers needed every bit of that production. The team required overtime to defeat the 1-5 Buccaneers 26-19. In the victory, Metcalf was one of only two wideouts to catch a pass.

The big game is something for Metcalf to build on going forward. But NFL analyst Gregg Rosenthal isn't sure the veteran is still the top option in the Steelers passing game.

This week, Rosenthal argued that is now Pittsburgh's sensational rookie Germie Bernard. who also had 11 catches against the Buccaneers.

"Watch Germie Bernard for the Steelers," Rosenthal said on his NFL Daily podcast , via Steelers Now's Aaron Becker . "A rookie that Aaron Rodgers absolutely trusts and can do a little bit of everything really well.

When I saw the deceleration and his ability to go from full speed to stopping in a second, it reminded me of Chris Olave . Not saying he's going to be Chris Olave. He doesn't have that juice, but a little more juice than expected.

I look at him as the 1A, and DK Metcalf right now, coming off his best game of the year, as the 1B."

Bernard caught the game-winning touchdown in overtime against the Buccaneers. The rookie has reached at least 80 receiving yards in each of the past two contests.

Metcalf had 93 receiving yards on his 11 receptions Sunday.

Is Steelers' D.K. Metcalf Giving Way to Rookie Germie Bernard?

Metcalf hasn't been very consistent this season. Particularly early in the year, he dealt with drops.

The veteran broke out of his funk with five catches and 115 yards versus the Cleveland Browns in Week 4. But he then followed that up with just three receptions for 12 yards in Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts .

Still, it's a little hard to believe a pundit would suggest Metcalf isn't still quarterback Aaron Rodgers's favorite target.

Even with Bernard coming on the past couple weeks, Metcalf has received 20 more targets than the rookie this season. Metcalf also leads the Steelers with 30 catches and 318 receiving yards.

Only running back Jaylen Warren has more yards from scrimmage for the team.

Rosenthal's hot take about Bernard moving ahead of Metcalf could say more about Bernard than Metcalf.

The rookie has been incredible the past couple games, which is notable considering how difficult Rodgers has been on first-year receivers in the past.

Clearly, Bernard has earned the future Hall of Fame quarterback's trust. That's a great sign for the Steelers receiver room.

With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson both on injured reserve, it doesn't really matter who's the top receiver in the pecking order. The Steelers need both Metcalf and Bernard to produce on a weekly basis.

articles.title: I will never walk away from Boston - Hurst
articles.summary: Paul Hurst's Boston are 21st in the National League after three wins in 13 matches.
articles.body:
Boston manager Paul Hurst has said he would "never walk away" from his job, despite going through a difficult period at the club.

The Pilgrims have won just three of their opening 13 matches in the National League, and sit inside the relegation places in 21st.

Hurst spoke strongly after their FA Cup exit to fellow fifth tier strugglers Scunthorpe United last week, saying: "I'm not good enough, the players aren't good enough."

However, the 52-year-old told BBC Radio Lincolnshire he has no plans to quit.

"I wouldn't be sat here doing an interview If I did," he said. "I'd have a conversation with the chairman. I'm never going to walk away from a job, that's not in my nature.

"In a slightly sick way, I enjoy a challenge. My life, career - and I don't mean a big sob story at all - is built on showing resilience, fight, determination and attitude to try and prove people wrong.

"That's always been a driving force, that's not going to change. Do I get really frustrated at times? Absolutely, I'm human. But I came back to this football club for the people, and because its full-time."

Hurst spent 22 months in joint charge of Boston between 2009 and 2011, leading them up into the National League North before leaving to join National League Grimsby.

He returned in January 2026 with Boston 17th in the table, four places and three points above the relegation places, and led them to a 12th-placed finish.

Hurst said he is determined to stay on and improve the club: "Ultimately, when I do leave this club it would be fantastic if it was on my terms, we all know often that's not the case.

"It would be trying to leave this club in a better place and I think some of that is happening, but unfortunately the league table and the results aren't really showing that at the moment.

"People will need to put trust and belief in what I'm saying. They're not in here every day seeing the improvements, and you have to improve to keep up with the other teams in the league.

"I will always give my all for this football club. It's great if you can win with skill, but if you can't you win with will. I thought against Southend we got quite a bit of that".

articles.title: Leader of the Pack

articles.body:
Lauren Bissen has been with the Glacier cross country team for four seasons and if it seems longer, it's probably because she has finished in the top three at a Montana high school meet 24 times.

Outwardly, she hasn't changed much. She entered the stage as a blonde, slight, bespectacled freshman who ran beyond her strides; about the only difference now is all the colleges that lined up to give her a scholarship.

"She showed up with a lot more confidence than in year's past," Glacier Wolfpack coach Cody Moore said. "She's always been confident, but this year it has kind of bleached into everything else. We have a really young team, and I think her legacy will be finished by those younger girls. She definitely left her mark."

Both the Glacier boys and girls are projected to finish in the top three at Saturday's State AA Cross Country Championship, run in concert with the other three classes at Amend Park in Billings. That's a high-water mark in Moore's seven years leading the program; the girls finished fourth the last two seasons, and the boys were fifth in 2025.

"I think that's really exciting," Bissen said. "We have a really strong group this year — and young, too, which is also exciting. It's been fun to see the progress.

"I'm really proud of the group this year. We're really close and it's so fun to hang out with and work hard with them. I'm lucky to be on the team that I'm on."

Moore feels fortunate as well. He hadn't been on the job long when Bissen arrived, starting an upward trend for a squad that finished ninth out of 16 teams at state in 2022. With Bissen taking second as a freshman, the Pack jumped to fifth the next October.

"She showed up as a freshman and has been remarkably consistent since," Moore said. "She's just so studious and curious about getting better. She always asked about the why behind what we're doing and it's all due to her being curious about getting better."

Here's a curious fact: Bissen was running the fastest times of anyone not named Addison Kegel for most of last season, but someone was closing the gap. It was teammate Ada Thiel, who surged at the end to win last year's State AA title as a freshman.

"It was a surprise to everyone," Moore said. "And it speaks to Lauren's character. Obviously there were those initial 20 seconds of disappointment, but then she was hugging her and they were holding hands on the awards stand.

"You don't want to lose a race, but if you do you'd want it to be to your best friend and training partner."

"She ran a great race," Bissen said. "It was a really strong race. I was also surprised — I hadn't expected her to come from behind. But in the end, that's racing. And then it was, 'OK. Now let's think about the next race.' "

The next race was the Nike Cross Country Northwest Regionals: She finished in 17 minutes, 39.8 seconds, a career best.

"Last year to break 18 minutes was a big deal for her, and she's been consistently under that this season," Moore said.

Colleges came calling, and last week Bissen committed to Boise State. She has a goal of medical school; in the immediate future she'd like to see the Pack bring home some hardware. She and Thiel make a dynamic 1-2 punch; Bissen wants to chase down a great finish to a high school career full of them.

"I'd set some big goals for this season: Devote more energy and focus and be real intentional — a better teammate, better person and be a better competitor," she said. "It's still a work in progress; the season isn't over yet.

"But yeah, I have been intentional and working hard. And yes, it has been a great season."

Diego Leon's agent has revealed that they will be exploring a move elsewhere if the player is not granted any first-team minutes between now and the end of 2026.

The 19-year-old has yet to make his Manchester United debut since signing from Cerro Porteno in a deal worth up to £7 million.

Leon has been featuring prominently with the Under-21s, but is seemingly chomping at the bit to be called up to the senior squad and stake his claim.

The fact that United are facing a crisis in his position at left-back has likely prompted his agent to go public with the youngster's desire to feature under Michael Carrick, as it would provide one more option in Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu's absences.

However, fellow academy star and left-back Harry Amass was kept at Old Trafford over the summer for depth, but Noussair Mazraoui and even Diogo Dalot have been preferred in the role in recent weeks, showing Carrick is opting for experience.

"If there isn't a plan to break into the first team between December and January, we'll look for a way out for him. A loan somewhere where he can compete, get playing time, and return to Manchester," said Leon's representative, Renato Bittar (via Sport Witness ).

"The Championship is an option, as are other European leagues, but we don't want to leave here. He's performing well with the U21 team, he's training well, and his physical condition is excellent."

There may be more options for Leon to earn some minutes when United kick off their FA Cup campaign in the coming months, though their premature Carabao Cup exit may have convinced Carrick to go full-strength in order to avoid another embarrassment.

articles.title: Why the Falcons need to prioritize Kyle Pitts to solve passing game woes
articles.summary: It’s another season where a coaching staff has to figure out how to consistently utilize the dynamic pass-catcher.
articles.body:
With less than 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, Kyle Pitts caught his second pass on a quick out as the Falcons trailed 31-7. It's normally a standard route and play for a tight end to make in a lopsided matchup. It became the spark the Falcons needed for an unexpected comeback attempt. It also could prove to be the platform to help combat one of the most pressing issues surrounding the Falcons.

The Bears soundly outplayed them in every phase of the game, making it an uncompetitive matchup at one point in the second half. The defensive front got bulldozed out of gaps and struggled to maintain its rush integrity against Caleb Williams. The special teams were an absolute disaster, headlined by Zachariah Branch's nightmare performance that every rookie dreads.

Despite those glaring shortcomings and breakdowns, the most damaging aspect of the loss was how overwhelmed the offense looked against Chicago's pressure looks.

For the second consecutive game, Michael Penix Jr. looked incapable of making the right reads and throwing accurately under pressure for long stretches. The coaching staff's game plan to combat Dennis Allen's constant schemed-up pressures should raise plenty of questions.

Penix Jr. still could have operated better with quicker processing and better feel for blindside pressure. It took until the fourth quarter for him to find some rhythm against Chicago's defense when they rushed five or six.

That's when Penix Jr. connected with Jahan Dotson for 32 yards on a stop route, where Dotson made a nice hesitation move that turned a solid completion into an explosive gain. It was a sharp play beating Chicago's five-man pressure.

Dotson's career inconsistency and overall limitations make you cautious about his ability to create separation on the outside often enough to give Penix Jr. high-percentage looks against blitzes. What Pitts did on the next play can be replicated, albeit hopefully not as dramatically for the sake of the Falcons.

Per Pro Football Focus, Pitts ran 17 routes from the slot versus Chicago. That was a season high, easily surpassing the seven he ran against Carolina. Some of the high usage from the slot can be attributed to the game script. It was the first game this season where the Falcons were behind all game long with Penix Jr. under center. That proved to be a recipe for success after three quarters of a mostly inept dropback passing game.

Chicago brought six with former Falcon Clark Phillips rushing in unblocked. Penix Jr. had to get the ball out quickly again to Pitts outside the numbers. The throw was inside of Pitts, allowing Elijah Hicks to close in for a potential interception. Somehow, the 2025 second-team All-Pro tight end ripped the ball away and juked past Nick McCloud to produce a remarkable 29-yard gain. In the process, he prevented a certain turnover with his improved contested-catch ability.

Those types of completions could be an instant solution to the Falcons' problems against crowded fronts and blitzes. Whether defenses only rush four or bring the entire house with seven or somewhere in between, Baltimore and Chicago have provided a blueprint to rattle Penix Jr. by crowding the line of scrimmage with bodies.

Combine that with Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees falling short of answers schematically, and you get a dropback passing game that severely limits the offense. That can't happen against top-tier teams like the Ravens and Bears.

Three plays after the highlight-reel reception, Pitts was in the slot again on third down. Chicago rushed six, with Allen being relentless in trying to force Penix Jr. into another off-target throw or sack. Instead, the young quarterback found Pitts uncovered, as Hicks couldn't make up the ground to stop him. It was a routine touchdown, but it showed how Pitts can be a dependable solution to a glaring problem.

Despite being such a unique talent as a deep threat, Pitts can be maximized in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. He proved last year that he can consistently make defenders miss and run through contact after the catch. His blocking has improved enough that he can play more in-line and create more mismatches with his explosiveness off the line of scrimmage.

While he should be used more in the slot following Olamide Zaccheaus' poor play and Branch's disastrous game, Pitts can also line up more traditionally as a tight end to bolster the Falcons' aerial attack.

After Jessie Bates connected on his signature peanut punch to force a fumble, as he does multiple times a year, it didn't take long for Penix Jr. to go back to Pitts. Operating in no-huddle, they slowed Chicago's pressure plan and capitalized on Pitts being isolated inside with an undersized defensive back.

Targeting that mismatch helped Penix Jr. find Pitts to convert on third and nine. They connected again on the next play to get in the end zone, putting the Falcons within striking distance of an outrageous comeback. A slight rub by Zaccheaus on the slant-flat concept gave Pitts the space necessary to score his second touchdown of the game.

As much as fans want to see Pitts be utilized like the unicorn he was projected to be, the coaching staff needs him more than ever as a possession pass-catcher in these situations to give Penix Jr. an immediate option under pressure.

There will be instances where he can thrive in the slot, like against Chicago. He could also line up as an in-line tight end, chipping an edge rusher and serving as a reliable outlet underneath. Whatever the play design, Pitts needs to be a bigger focal point to make the passing game more efficient.

According to TruMedia, the Bears blitzed Penix Jr. on an alarming 48.7 percent of his dropbacks. That could increase in upcoming matchups against Todd Bowles, Steve Spagnuolo, and Brian Flores. Those coaches won't hesitate to ramp up the pressure on any quarterback, let alone a young passer who isn't reacting well when seven defenders are lined up across the line of scrimmage.

The coaching staff will have to do its share schematically to solidify their protection plan. Making Pitts a bigger focal point in the passing game is the other vital step to punish defenses for constantly blitzing. Signs are emerging in recent weeks, as Pitts' target share has increased over the last three games.

That said, those targets have to come earlier in games. Pitts catching only his second pass late in what was arguably the Falcons' most disappointing performance of the season (with a starting-caliber quarterback under center) indicates he needs to be prioritized far more early and often.

As expected, Texas EDGE Colin Simmons is out for the Longhorns game against Ole Miss . But now his backup Richard Wesley is out as well. To make matters worse, starting running back Hollywood Smothers is doubtful when UT hosts the Rebels.

It's never a good time to be without your best player, but when the game is as important as Saturday night's matchup with Mississippi, it will make the challenge even tougher.

With Wesley out too, defensive coordinator Will Muschamp will have a huge hole to fill in the lineup. Especially since the Rebels have arguably the best quarterback in the nation under center in Trinidad Chambliss.

articles.title: CBS Sports puts Indiana on upset alert against Michigan football
articles.summary: Michigan football faces Indiana this Saturday with renewed hope as quarterback Tommy Carr sparks an upset alert.
articles.body:
Not many people are giving Michigan football much of a chance to beat Indiana on Saturday, especially with the Hoosiers coming off a loss. But given that the Wolverines came alive offensively in the second half, when they moved off Bryce Underwood in favor of Tommy Carr, anything can happen.

And with renewed hope on that side of the ball, there's a chance, albeit a slight one.

The Hoosiers lost to Ohio State in a game they probably should have won, and Michigan had to hang on for dear life against a moribund Penn State team. But CBS Sports' Brad Crawford has seen enough to at least say, hey, the Wolverines have enough of a chance that IU is officially on notice, as he put Indiana on upset alert .

At what point will Michigan's offense put together a full game? Is that even possible for the Wolverines? Saturday's chore comes in the form of Indiana , an elite team with a defense aiming to deny Michigan any semblance of confidence on that side of the field. Tommy Carr is the better option at quarterback, and there's limited film on him for Bryant Haines and the Hoosiers' defensive staff. This was included in this week's upset alert because the betting line screams competitive game. And twice this season, Indiana has failed to push away from league competition on the road despite winning ( Northwestern and Nebraska ). It's a must-win for Indiana if the Hoosiers intend on getting a top-four seed in the CFP.

articles.title: Former Colts RB Marshall Faulk reveals Parkinson's disease diagnosis
articles.summary: Former Indianapolis Colts running back Marshall Faulk revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.
articles.body:
Former Indianapolis Colts running back Marshall Faulk revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

Faulk discussed the diagnosis with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar on 'The Caring Neurologist' podcast.

"He (Faulk) said that with medication, he is not experiencing 'issues' beyond hand rigidity," ESPN's Alex Scarborough wrote , "which he believes hasn't gotten worse in the year and a half he has been dealing with the disease, and 'little tremors.'"

Faulk first noticed that something was off when he experienced "rigidity" in his hands after golfing. Faulk added that he feels "clear of thought," with no cognitive decline.

Faulk spent his first five seasons with the Colts . There he rushed for 5,320 yards and 42 touchdowns. He then played his next seven seasons with the St. Louis Rams.

Faulk is a member of the Hall of Fame and the Colts' Ring of Honor.

He is currently the football coach at Southern University.

articles.title: Opelousas football outlast Cecilia in a Week 8 thriller between rivals
articles.summary: Opelousas and Cecilia football put on a show in a Thursday Night Lights edition of this rivalry between 337 powerhouses. Here are the takeaways.
articles.body:
Every time Opelousas and Cecilia football face off, you'd better grab some popcorn.

The 2026 meeting between the Tigers and Bulldogs was another production, as momentum shifted all night long in the Week 8 matchup.

The Opelousas sideline went through a flurry of emotions with the lead changing countless time at Donald Garnder Staduim. Nearly 100 points scored later, the Tigers were the ones to come out on top, sneaking past the Bulldogs for a 50-48 victory.

"This rivalry is rich, and we knew we had to help the seniors win this with this being the final home game of the regular season," Opelousas running back Joseph Clues said. "We had to secure the win, and we just executed the plays that coach gave us."

It wasn't a pretty victory for Opelousas, but it'll go down as statement win, handing Cecilia its first loss in district play. With this win, the Tigers have now opened the doors for a possible three-way tie for the Class 4A District 5 championship.

Fans could tell Opelousas was eager to face off against Cecilia after last year's disappointing loss. On Cecilia's first offensive play of the drive, Opelousas senior Jaylon Owens landed a big hit on the Bulldogs quarterback, forcing a fumble. That set the tone for the rest of the night for the Tigers.

Owens went on to be the Tigers' leading receivers, tallying approximately 100 yards, a touchdown and three 2-point conversions. Whenever senior quarterback Collin Rideau needed an outlet, Owens was there along with senior Caden Arvie, who finished with approximately 80 yards receiving and a touchdown.

The star of the Tigers' offense however, was Clues, who didn't start the game due to being a bit banged up from last week.

"He was nursing some injuries, but he gave me the sign that he was good to go," Opelousas coach Harry Coleman said on Clues. "He warmed up real good, and he got out there and he showed what he is, man. He's the workhorse of this team, and we're gonna ride him."

Clues ran all night long, rushing for approximately 245 yards and four touchdowns on 28 carries. If the Bulldogs gave him a sliver of room, he squeezed through for big play after big play.

Dirty laundry was a theme of the matchup for both teams with Opelousas racking up double-digit penalties in the first half alone. While the Tigers had more penalties against them, the penalties against Cecilia proved more costly in such a close game.

"We left a lot on the table, and I'm sure they think the same way, but just the little things that hurt us when it's time," Cecilia coach Cody Champange said. "If we would have caught the 2-point conversion, if we don't muff the punt. We've got to clean those things up in a game like this."

In defeat, the Bulldogs never quit, with senior running back Deondre Briscoe leading their scoring with four rushing touchdowns. With this loss, Cecilia will have to now beat Carencro to force a three-way tie for district championship between itself, the Golden Bears and the Tigers.

articles.title: Daily Bean: Bruins Win; McDavid Makes History; Hellebuyck Suspension Ends Today
articles.summary: The Boston Bruins put up six for their sixth win in seven games. The Bruins cruised past the Nashville Predators […]
articles.body:
The Boston Bruins put up six for their sixth win in seven games.

The Bruins cruised past the Nashville Predators last night, extending their point streak to seven games with a 6-0 win. Michael DiPietro made 28 saves for his first NHL shutout, but the night carried a little more meaning than that milestone.

Elsewhere around the league, we're seeing a lot of Connor. The one in Edmonton made history, while the one in Winnipeg (for now?) will see his suspension end today. There is a trade board, a report on a Blue Jackets left winger, and an update from Kyle Dubas on Ben Kindel. The Flyers may have some expendable trade pieces, and a couple of goalies made their debut last night.

Happy Friday, catch up on Bruins and league news in today's Daily Bean :

BRUINS WIN : The Bruins (8-2-1) extended their point streak to seven with a 6-0 thumping of the Nashville Predators (3-3-3). David Pastrnak scored twice, Charlie McAvoy finished with four assists, and Michael DiPietro made 28 saves for his first NHL shutout. Five different Bruins found the back of the net in the win.

POSTGAME : Michael DiPietro's first shutout came on a pretty meaningful night. The Bruins hosted Hockey Fights Cancer night on Thursday, and DiPietro, who lost his mother to cancer when he was five, spoke about what the milestone meant to him and his family.

Ahead of warmups last night, the Bruins placed a jersey on their bench in memory of Alex Gimenez, the Bruins' director of hockey operations, collective bargaining agreement, who passed away after a battle with cancer in September.

In memory of our teammate, Alex Gimenez 💜 pic.twitter.com/J9oiGP9zF6 — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 22, 2026

In memory of our teammate, Alex Gimenez 💜 pic.twitter.com/J9oiGP9zF6

Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 22, 2026

NEXT UP : The Bruins have the day off today. They will hold a morning skate at TD Garden before closing the season series with San Jose tomorrow night.

Sportsnet : Another night, another milestone for Connor McDavid . He's up to 30 points in 10 games, becoming the fourth player in NHL history to hit that mark, joining Wayne Gretzky , Mario Lemieux , and Mike Bossy . He also had another five-point outing, and he and Lemieux are the only two players in league history to have three five-point nights in the first 10 games of a season.

McDavid is on pace (and I say this very lightly) for 260 points this season.

TSN : Today is the day Connor Hellebuyck 's suspension is lifted, and he has to complete a physical in order to be restored to the active roster. The Jets play in the Heritage Classic on Sunday, and Darren Dreger reported that there could be an agreement to postpone Hellebuyck's physical until after the game "out of respect to the Heritage Classic."

Sportsnet : Trade board! Why not? It's still early, but Nick Kypreos released the second trade board of the season. Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin obviously dominate the headline, but a few Bruins (one current and two former) made it to the list.

TSN : The Blue Jackets are taking calls on Dmitri Voronkov , according to Pierre LeBrun. Voronkov has two assists in six games this season, and he finished last season with 32 points (17-15–32) in 63 games. He is signed for the rest of the season at $4.175M and will be an RFA this summer.

Philly Hockey Now : The Flyers have rattled off three straight wins after losing their first eight, and their young players have been a big part of the turnaround. Will James looks at whether the youth movement could make some veterans expendable.

Pittsburgh Hockey Now : Penguins GM Kyle Dubas provided an update on forward Ben Kindel yesterday. The 19-year-old collapsed 10 minutes into the Penguins' flight home with what was diagnosed as a vasovagal episode. Kindel returned to Pittsburgh and will go through the NHL's return-to-play protocols. Dan Kingerski was there and has the update on Kindel.

Montreal Hockey Now : Nick Suzuki will miss 2-to-4 weeks with an upper-body injury, the Canadiens announced. Marc Dumont writes that this is the "ultimate stress test," with the injury to the captain coming at a bad time for a team off to an underwhelming start.

Florida Hockey Now : Cooper Black is tall. Like, Chara tall. Black became the tallest goaltender (6-foot-9) to suit up in an NHL game when he made his debut for the Florida Panthers last night. It did not go so well, as the Panthers could not find the back of the net and were handed their second loss in as many nights .

Detroit Hockey Now : Speaking of goalie debuts, Michal Postava also made his last night. The Red Wings' goaltender got his first NHL minutes in the third period of Detroit's 5-2 win over Vancouver last night, jumping in for the injured John Gibson after 40 minutes.

And just one more on goalies: what an unbelievable save by Yaroslav Askarov last night.

articles.title: Bold predictions in NFL Week 7: Jahmyr Gibbs, Ja’Marr Chase & more
articles.summary: Bold predictions for 3 of the league's biggest stars in Week 7.
articles.body:
Every NFL Sunday produces a number that makes you check whether the television graphic is broken. Sometimes it is. Sometimes a great player has spent three hours making the production crew double-check its work.

Week 7 offers a few chances to get ahead of that confusion, with sound football reasons behind the absurd numbers. Let's put numbers on it and make some predictions.

Jahmyr Gibbs reaches 100 rushing yards and 100 receiving yards against the Packers

Detroit can keep Gibbs's handoffs coming while crossers, double moves and wider alignments test coverage assignments against Jonathan Gannon's shifting fronts. Gibbs averages 21 carries and 100.8 rushing yards per game. His first three games included 15 slot or wide alignments, up from three in the same span last season.

Green Bay allows just 34 receiving yards per game to backs, and Gibbs's receiving high is 65. Jared Goff can attack farther downfield and let Gibbs create after the catch while preserving his rushing workload. The carries stay; the routes do the extra damage.

Ja'Marr Chase catches 3 touchdown passes against the Ravens

Baltimore allows just 3.8 yards per carry, giving Joe Burrow reasons to finish drives through the air. Moving Chase across formations can create opportunities, while Tee Higgins and the tight ends keep defenders occupied elsewhere. Burrow threw four touchdowns to four receivers against Miami before Cincinnati's bye, including Chase's 45-yard score.

This time, Chase gets greedy. He already caught three touchdown passes against the Ravens in 2024. Give him one strike from distance, then let his release and Burrow's placement add two more near the goal line.

Derek Stingley Jr. intercepts 2 passes against the Giants

Malik Nabers's 42 targets over the Giants' last three games give Stingley a clear tendency to study as J.J. McCarthy makes his first Giants start. Stingley needn't shadow Nabers; he can attack when those routes enter his coverage, and pressure rushes the throw.

McCarthy has 13 interceptions in 12 career appearances, while Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter have combined for 10.5 sacks this season. Stingley has no picks this year, but he took two from Miami in December 2024. One hurried throw, and another forced attempt can make the new quarterback's introduction considerably less pleasant.

articles.title: Knicks used empty promises of championship rings to trick employees into clicking a phishing link
articles.summary: James Dolan's stinginess — and passion for surveillance and cybersecurity — knows no bounds.
articles.body:
The Knicks danced in confetti in June, relishing their first title in a generation off the backs of Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mike Brown and more.

Four months on, a lot of the goodwill that seemed to fall at the feet of New York owner James Dolan for his willingness to bankroll that title-winning unit appears to have vanished.

The 71-year-old has drawn the ire of many basketball enthusiasts in recent decades. A Trump acolyte who was forced to settle a dispute with a former Knicks executive who alleged that he fired her after filing a sexual harassment report against former New York president Isiah Thomas, Dolan is hardly a popular figure in sports.

He didn't do himself any favors with the his latest trick, one that saw him fool masses of Madison Square Garden employees hoping to get a chance to deck their fingers in gold after New York's championship triumph.

Here's what you need to know about the Knicks phishing scandal that took social media by storm.

Knicks championship ring cybersecurity test

Dolan's passion for surveillance is well-documented at this point. Madison Square Garden has been less a sporting venue that a panopticon for Dolan, wrote Wired's Noah Shachtman and Robert Silverman in April 2026. The pairing, alongside investigative journalist Pablo Torre , helped reveal the extent of Dolan's obsession with cybersecurity, detailing how, among other things, Dolan's security staff harassed and "obsessively tracked" a trans woman over a two-year period.

Perhaps it's unsurprising, then, to see Dolan and Co. return to the well once more, this time directing their efforts towards their own employees.

Dolan's company picked quite the ruse as a trojan horse to pursue its obsession with biometrics. The Athletic's Joe Vardon detailed the scope of Dolan's fixation in an article that came out Thursday. Vardon reported that the Knicks governor reportedly sent an email to employees vowing to offer them the choice of a potential championship ring.

"Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here," the email read, per The Athletic.

"[Employee name], this one is on the house. MSG is issuing a complimentary employee championship ring. The same jeweler, the same craftsmanship, personalized with your name. No cost to you.

"There are two designs to choose from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic. Reserve the one you want below."

The email was a scam, however. The message was actually a phishing test, used to see if Madison Square Garden employees would click on the link featured at the bottom of the page. If they did, they were greeted not with jewelry, but with a mandatory cybersecurity class, per Vardon.

Did Knicks employees actually get championship rings?

Many longtime employees at Madison Square Garden employees are not expected to receive a championship ring for their troubles, per Vardon. Dolan has shown an unwillingness to part ways with his hordes of money over the years; ESPN's Shams Charania reported that New York's latest contract extension offer to star big Karl-Anthony Towns is worth more than $75 million less than he's eligible for.

Dolan's unwillingness to give just rewards to players who have served his franchise dutifully appears to be a window into his frugality. Predictably, that stinginess is also reserved for mere mortals, including those that make up the masses of the Madison Square Garden workforce.

Others subjected to the whims of the Dolan's parsimony appear to include select New York assistants, who have not yet received their signets.

Online reaction to Knicks championship ring cybersecurity test

articles.summary: Ranking all 15 Eastern Conference NBA teams.
articles.body:
The NBA has finally returned, and the Eastern Conference is already proving to be unpredictable. In just three days, the reigning champs have fallen, a flurry of blowouts took place, and contenders scrapped against each other for their first wins. There's plenty to unpack from week one, but these early power rankings display the parity among the East.

Brooklyn lost its home opener to Charlotte. Both Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle played well, with Randle putting up 33 points and MPJ adding 26. Both players shot efficiently, but it wasn't enough to get the Nets a win. Brooklyn is a young team with plenty of room to grow, but it has a long way to go.

The Bulls were blown out by Toronto in their season opener. Playing on the road against a very good team is a tough environment, but it's still concerning that Chicago trailed by as many as 48 points. With a revamped roster and front office, the Bulls are a young team that will likely need some time to grow.

The Bucks lost to the Washington Wizards on the road in their season opener. Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. led the way, each putting up more than 20 points. Milwaukee looked better than expected, especially considering it was an away game. However, losing to Washington is still concerning, given that the Wizards aren't expected to be very good this season.

Charlotte took down the Brooklyn Nets in New York to open its season. No one player stood out, as multiple Hornets finished with around 20 points. Beating what could be the worst team in the conference isn't necessarily impressive, but getting the job done on the road is still a solid start for Charlotte.

Orlando lost to Atlanta in its home opener despite a phenomenal performance from Paolo Banchero. Banchero finished with 35 points, seven rebounds and 10 assists while missing just two shots. The Magic played well but still came up short, which is concerning for a team with high expectations entering the season.

The Wizards took down the Milwaukee Bucks in their home opener, winning by 12 points. However, beating a struggling Milwaukee team at home isn't the most convincing way to start the season. Anthony Davis led the way with 34 points, while Trae Young added 20 points and 13 assists. Washington got the job done, but it will need to prove itself against tougher competition.

Tyrese Haliburton made his return to the court as the Pacers opened their season against the New Orleans Pelicans. Indiana escaped with a three-point win in a nail-biter. Pascal Siakam led the way with 35 points, while Haliburton finished with 23 points and 12 assists. If Haliburton can return to form, Indiana could be a team to watch in the Eastern Conference.

Atlanta took down the Orlando Magic on the road to open its season. The Hawks were led by an unlikely 31-point performance from Nickeil Alexander-Walker. Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels also chipped in 20 points apiece. Atlanta earned an impressive road win against a team with playoff aspirations, giving the Hawks an encouraging start to the season.

Miami was manhandled by the Minnesota Timberwolves in its season opener. The Heat have some talented pieces, but this roster doesn't appear to be built for a championship run. With Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo in the mix, Miami has the potential to be a difficult matchup for opposing teams. However, the Heat have plenty to prove after their opening-night performance.

Boston lost its season opener against Detroit in a game that raised some early concerns. Surprisingly, Paul George looked like the best offseason signing in the league, putting up 38 points in an impressive performance. Meanwhile, Mitchell Robinson struggled to make an impact, raising questions about his fit. Jayson Tatum also had an ugly shooting night, going 6-for-23 from the field. Boston has plenty of talent, but it will need more consistency to compete with the East's best.

Toronto blew out Chicago in its season opener, establishing itself as a team to watch early in the season. The Bulls aren't a terrible roster on paper, making the Raptors' performance even more impressive. Toronto led by as many as 48 points, while four players finished with at least 20 points. It was a dominant showing from a team looking to make some noise in the Eastern Conference.

Cleveland lost to Philadelphia in its season opener, but playing on the road against one of the conference's top teams is no easy task. Donovan Mitchell and Tyrese Maxey matched each other with 32 points apiece in an entertaining matchup. The Cavaliers have the talent to compete with the East's best, but they'll need to bounce back after a tough opening-night loss.

Detroit opened its season with an impressive win over a talented Boston Celtics team at home. Cade Cunningham led the way, while Jalen Duren looked great after a lackluster playoff performance last season. The Pistons made a statement by taking down one of the conference's top teams, giving fans reason to be optimistic about what's ahead.

The Knicks lost at home to what could be the best team in the league. Despite the loss, New York didn't look bad, but Philadelphia proved to be too much. The Knicks have the talent to compete with anyone in the Eastern Conference, and one loss against a championship contender shouldn't change that. Still, they'll need to bounce back quickly to keep pace with the conference's best.

The Philadelphia 76ers have wasted no time making a statement with their new-look roster featuring LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. Philadelphia took down the Knicks in New York before returning home to defeat the Cleveland Cavaliers in its second game. Starting the season 2-0 with wins over two of the East's top teams is an impressive way to open the year. If Philadelphia can maintain this level of play, it could be the team to beat in the Eastern Conference.

articles.title: USC Trojans needs its stars to be ready on the road at Wisconsin
articles.summary: USC football's momentum going into the Ohio State and Indiana games will be shaped by what the Trojans do in Wisconsin
articles.body:
Usually, a game against the Wisconsin Badgers on the road would strike fear in USC fans. This time around, that might not be the case, as USC football has its sights set on much bigger competition. Winning on the road against Penn State a few weeks ago showed this team is more than capable of getting it done. USC should pass its next road test this week with flying colors.

Here is how Week 8 will play out for the USC Trojans against the Wisconsin Badgers :

King Miller and Waymond Jordan both will be key contributors

The Badgers historically have been a program that specializes in running the football. This season, their quarterback has been the driving force behind their run game. The Trojans will have the more imposing run game in this football game. King Miller will run for 100 yards, and Waymond Jordan will bully the Badgers' defense when he gets his opportunity. The run game will set the tone early for USC and also put the game away late in the second half.

Zacharyus Williams will be the Trojans leading receiver this week

The Wisconsin Badgers best unit on their defense is their secondary. Their secondary will put its best effort into shutting down the two freshman stud receivers for USC. That will open the door for Zacharyus Williams to burn the Badgers deep for multiple big plays. I think Williams will lead the Trojans in receiving yards as he goes for 100 yards and a touchdown.

Colton Joseph will throw 2 interceptions

Colton Joseph has kept the turnovers down, but against the Trojans' defense, he will try to play hero ball way more than he should. Kennedy Urlacher and Christian Pierce will both get interceptions in this game and help things swing into USC's favor big time.

Jahkeem Stewart will get his first sack of the season

Jahkeem Stewart's impact has been felt greatly since his return. He returned a fumble for a touchdown against the Washington Huskies to seal the deal, and he has been a great interior disruptor. Against the Wisconsin Badgers, Stewart will get after Joseph and bring him down for his first sack of the season. This will be Stewart's official breakout game. He will play a big part in ensuring Joseph does not dominate the Trojans with his legs.

USC has played to the level of their competition; no better example than the game against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights. Against Wisconsin, USC will put it all together. The Trojans' offense will play to the level they should, and the defense will follow suit with a complementary performance. USC will get a statement on the road, winning 38-17.
